# reminder-producer implementation plan Ã¢â‚¬â€ Round 3 (Claude revision)

Responds to Codex round 2 (6.2/10, `round-2-codex-output.txt`, 13 required changes). Everything
from round 1/2 NOT contradicted here stands unchanged (names in round-1 Ã‚Â§1, error taxonomy
conclusion that no new `AppError` subclass is needed, most of round-2's port/schema-file-location
corrections). This round's central fix: **the checkpoint-before-continuation ordering bug (required
changes 1+2) is resolved by using this codebase's OWN transactional outbox pattern for the
checkpoint transition** Ã¢â‚¬â€ the same mechanism `producer.ts:264-306` already uses for
claimÃ¢â€ â€™dispatch, applied one layer up, to scan-pageÃ¢â€ â€™continuation. Round 2's own "outbox doesn't
apply here, there's no aggregate write" reasoning (round 1 Ã‚Â§4) was the actual mistake: **the lease
row IS the aggregate being written at checkpoint time** Ã¢â‚¬â€ this was hiding in plain sight.

## Required changes 1+2: checkpoint/continuation Ã¢â‚¬â€ outbox-atomic, not send-then-checkpoint

**`SQS_REMINDER_SCAN_CONTINUATION_V1` is reinstated in `OutboxDestination`** (round 2 wrongly
removed it). Checkpoint transition (after a page's candidates are durably published, see Ã‚Â§7 below)
is now ONE `TransactWriteItems`, same shape as `producer.ts:286-306`:
```ts
const outboxEntries: DynamoTransactPutEntry[] = [];
appendToTransaction(outboxEntries, deps.tableName, continuationEvent, "SQS_REMINDER_SCAN_CONTINUATION_V1");
await deps.store.transactWrite([
  { Update: buildUnscopedVersionedUpdate({ tableName, key: leaseKey, expectedVersion: leaseVersionThisInvocationRead, set: { lastEvaluatedKey: nextKey /* or REMOVE + status: "COMPLETED" on last page */, leaseUntil: now + LEASE_MS, pagesProcessed: pagesProcessed + 1, candidatesPublished: candidatesPublished + thisPageCount }, extraConditions: [{ expression: "ownerToken = :myToken AND #startKeyCond", ... }] }) },
  ...outboxEntries,
]);
```
`DispatchOutboxRelay` (DynamoDB Streams, `producer.ts:270`'s existing mechanism) is extended to
also recognize `SQS_REMINDER_SCAN_CONTINUATION_V1` and publish to the scan queue instead of the
dispatch queue Ã¢â‚¬â€ same relay, same sweeper-recovers-publish-failures guarantee, routed by the
existing `destination` discriminator (no new relay Lambda). **Verified this round, not just
asserted**: `src/workers/dispatch-outbox-relay/relay.ts:12-14,22-27,122-152` shows the relay is
ALREADY a generalized multi-destination router (`senders: Record<OutboxDestination, Sender>`,
one sweeper instance covers multiple destinations) Ã¢â‚¬â€ it already recognizes
`SQS_REMINDER_DISPATCH_V1` and `SQS_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_V1` side by side, so adding a third
`senders` entry for `SQS_REMINDER_SCAN_CONTINUATION_V1` (pointing at the scan queue URL) is the
exact, already-precedented extension point Ã¢â‚¬â€ no relay redesign needed. **This closes required change 1's
exact failure trace**: a continuation now literally cannot exist in SQS until the checkpoint
transaction has committed, so "successor consumed before predecessor checkpoint" is impossible by
construction Ã¢â‚¬â€ there is no window where a successor can arrive early, because the successor's own
existence is downstream of (caused by) the checkpoint, not concurrent with it. Required change 2's
"specify a rigorous successor protocol" is answered by removing the need for one: at-least-once
delivery of the SAME continuation (streams relay redelivery, sweeper retry, or SQS standard-queue
redelivery) is idempotent because the checkpoint that produced it already advanced
`lastEvaluatedKey` Ã¢â‚¬â€ a redelivered continuation's handler re-reads the CURRENT lease row, finds
`lastEvaluatedKey` already matches (or is already past) what the message describes as "next to
process," and either does the work once (first delivery) or no-ops (subsequent redeliveries,
detected by comparing the message's OWN `lastEvaluatedKey` against the row's, exactly as round 2
proposed Ã¢â‚¬â€ this piece survives unchanged, now sitting on a sound foundation instead of a broken one).

**Cross-tenant envelope** (needed since `DomainEvent.tenantId: string` is non-optional,
`src/shared/contracts/events.ts:24`): continuation events use `tenantId: "SYSTEM"` Ã¢â‚¬â€ a documented
sentinel, precedented by this same file's existing `actor: { type: "SYSTEM" }` shape for
system-originated events (no new concept, reuses an existing "not a real tenant" convention this
codebase already has).

## Required change 3: work-unit enumeration Ã¢â‚¬â€ matches today's exact loop shape

Round 2 wrongly collapsed to "one message per shard." Corrected: the EventBridge-triggered
invocation reproduces `producer.ts:161-168`'s existing enumeration exactly Ã¢â‚¬â€ `lookback` (default 15,
`deps.lookbackMinutes ?? 15`, unchanged constant) inclusive minutes Ãƒâ€” `activeGenerations(shardConfig,
now)` (unchanged, handles legacy generations already) Ãƒâ€” that generation's shard partitions
(`gsi3PartitionsForMinute`, unchanged) Ã¢â‚¬â€ for EACH resulting (generation, shardId, minute) triple,
attempts a lease acquire and, if it wins (fresh or reclaim), sends ONE start message. A triple
whose lease is already `IN_PROGRESS`-unexpired or `COMPLETED` is skipped (no message sent) Ã¢â‚¬â€
exactly today's implicit "already done" behavior, now explicit. **Lease key now includes
generation**: `PK: SCAN#<shardFnVersion>#<shardId>#<minuteISO>`, `SK: LEASE` Ã¢â‚¬â€ collision-free
across reshard generations (round 2's gap, fixed). At `lookback=15` Ãƒâ€” up to 2 concurrent
generations (a reshard transition window) Ãƒâ€” 4 shards = up to 120 (generation,shard,minute) triples
evaluated per tick, but the vast majority are cheap `COMPLETED`-skip reads (already-finished older
minutes) Ã¢â‚¬â€ only the LATEST 1-2 minutes per (generation,shard) are ever genuinely `IN_PROGRESS`
under normal load, so real concurrent scan work stays bounded near `generations Ãƒâ€” shards` (Ã¢â€°Â¤8), not
120 (this bound feeds Ã‚Â§8's revised capacity numbers).

## Required change 4: message shapes Ã¢â‚¬â€ command-envelope for candidates, new system-envelope only for continuation

**Claim-candidate messages** (`SQS_REMINDER_CLAIM_CANDIDATE_V1`, NOT outbox-routed Ã¢â‚¬â€ no aggregate
transaction backs a raw GSI3 row) genuinely have a `tenantId` (parsed from `GSI3SK` before
publishing) and DO fit the existing `command-envelope.v1.json` shape unmodified: `commandType:
"reminder.claim-candidate.v1"`, `tenantId` (real tenant), `deduplicationKey:
"${tenantId}|${occurrenceId}|${pageOwnerToken}"`, `data: { occurrenceKey: {PK,SK}, entityType,
gsi3sk }`. New schema file `schemas/queues/reminder-claim-candidate.v1.json`:
`"allOf": [{ "$ref": "command-envelope.v1.json" }, { "properties": { "data": { "required":
["occurrenceKey","entityType","gsi3sk"], "properties": { "entityType": { "enum":
["ReminderOccurrence","DocumentChasingOccurrence"] }, ... } } } }]` Ã¢â‚¬â€ same `allOf` pattern as
`reminder-dispatch.v1.json:6-22` (re-read this round, confirmed shape).

**Scan-continuation messages** genuinely have no real tenant (cross-shard/tenant coordination) Ã¢â‚¬â€
forcing them into `command-envelope.v1.json` (which requires a real `tenantId`) would be a lie, so
a NEW `schemas/queues/system-envelope.v1.json` is added: same shape as `command-envelope.v1.json`
minus the `tenantId` requirement, plus a fixed `"tenantId": { "const": "SYSTEM" }` (kept present,
not dropped, so every queue message in this codebase has the same top-level field set Ã¢â‚¬â€ simpler
for any shared tooling that reads `tenantId` generically off an envelope, e.g. log correlation).
`schemas/queues/reminder-scan-continuation.v1.json` uses `allOf: [{"$ref":
"system-envelope.v1.json"}, ...]`, `data: { shardFnVersion, shardId, minute, ownerToken,
lastEvaluatedKey (nullable) }`. Both new schemas get valid+invalid fixtures added to the existing
consolidated `test/contract/schemas.test.ts` (round 2's correction, unchanged).

## Required change 5: sender-fault candidates Ã¢â‚¬â€ terminal, not dropped

Reversed from round 2: **any `SenderFault: true` entry in a `SendMessageBatch` response fails the
WHOLE page invocation** (throws after attempting the OTHER entries in that chunk, so
non-sender-fault entries still get their retry chance first) rather than being silently dropped.
This means the checkpoint transaction (Ã‚Â§1-2) never runs for that page, so no continuation is ever
produced for it Ã¢â‚¬â€ the chain is stuck `IN_PROGRESS` until `leaseUntil` expires, at which point the
NEXT eligible tick's reclaim (Ã‚Â§3) retries the ENTIRE page from the same `lastEvaluatedKey` (safe,
`queryGsi3Page` is a pure read). New metric `CandidateSenderFault` (Count, no dimensions) with an
alarm at >0 over any 5-minute period (fast detection Ã¢â‚¬â€ a sender fault means a real bug in candidate
construction, worth paging on immediately rather than waiting for the DLQ-age alarm's 1-hour
threshold). Retryable (non-sender-fault) entries: the ENTIRE original chunk is retried (not just
the failed IDs) using `nextAttemptDelayMs` (`outbox.ts:192-197`, reused as-is Ã¢â‚¬â€ same backoff
shape, not reinvented), capped at 3 attempts before the page throws as a transient failure (goes
through normal SQS-level retry of the scan/continuation message itself, `maxReceiveCount=5`).

## Required change 6: capacity Ã¢â‚¬â€ worst case is one shard/minute absorbing the full burst, not an even split

Corrected: 10,000 occurrences landing in a SINGLE (shard, minute) Ã¢â‚¬â€ not spread across shards Ã¢â‚¬â€ is
the real worst case (no proof of uniform hashing exists in this codebase, confirmed by round 2's
own finding; assuming otherwise was round 1/2's error). 10,000 ÃƒÂ· 200/page = 50 pages, chained
sequentially through outbox-relay hops. Each hop: checkpoint transaction (~50ms) + DynamoDB
Streams propagation to `DispatchOutboxRelay` (typically sub-second, occasionally a few seconds
under load Ã¢â‚¬â€ no repo measurement exists, so **2s is used as an explicit conservative per-hop
upper bound**, not a measured average) + SQS send + next invocation's cold/warm start. **50 hops Ãƒâ€”
~2.5s conservative-worst-case per hop Ã¢â€°Ë† 125s to fully drain a single-shard 10k burst** Ã¢â‚¬â€ stated as
an explicit bound, not an estimate dressed as a guarantee; still comfortably under the 5-minute
reconciliation threshold PERF-12 treats as the failure line, with the reasoning shown rather than
asserted.

**Scan Lambda timeout: revised to 90s** (one `queryGsi3Page` call + up to 20 `SendMessageBatch`
chunks of Ã¢â€°Â¤10 candidates each, each individually retryable per Ã‚Â§5 Ã¢â‚¬â€ 20 chunks Ãƒâ€” ~100ms typical +
margin for up to 3 chunks needing full 3-attempt backoff in a bad case Ã¢â€°Ë† 25s realistic worst case,
90s leaves >3x headroom) Ã¢â€ â€™ scan queue visibility timeout = 540s (module's fixed 6x). **Lease
duration: revised to 200s** (invariant: Ã¢â€°Â¥2Ãƒâ€” scan Lambda timeout = 180s Ã¢â€°Â¤ 200s; scan visibility
540s > 200s, preserving the no-redelivery-during-live-lease property with the new numbers). Claim
Lambda/queue unchanged from round 2 (10s timeout / 60s visibility).
**`reserved_concurrent_executions`**: scan queue = **10** (bound from Ã‚Â§3's Ã¢â€°Â¤8 genuinely-concurrent
chains + margin, explicit reasoning replacing round 1/2's "= shard count" oversimplification);
`maximum_concurrency` (event source mapping parameter) = 10, matching. Claim queue:
`reserved_concurrent_executions` = **50**, `maximum_concurrency` = 50 Ã¢â‚¬â€ sized against the
single-shard-burst model: 10,000 candidates ÃƒÂ· 10/batch = 1,000 claim-Lambda batches, at 50
concurrent Ãƒâ€” ~200ms/batch (this project's existing `reminder-dispatch` claim-shaped Lambda's own
observed latency class, reused as the estimate basis rather than an unmeasured guess) Ã¢â€°Ë† 4s of
processing time, arriving throughout the ~125s drain window, never backlogged. **`maxReceiveCount

(matches `reminder-dispatch`'s own existing event-source-mapping batch size,

numbers against that block in the final artifact). `MaximumBatchingWindowInSeconds`: 0 for scan

## Required change 7: error table Ã¢â‚¬â€ corrected reason-specific handling

Codex correctly found today's code treats ANY `TransactionCanceledException` as a lost race
(`producer.ts:309-314`, `document-chasing-producer.ts:112-135`), never inspecting
`getCancellationReasonCodes` (`occ.ts:431-447`) despite that helper existing Ã¢â‚¬â€ **this plan
deliberately does NOT preserve that behavior**, it fixes it, since D-299's own text names
"`CancellationReasons`, distinguindo corretamente" as a requirement of the new claim consumer, not
an optional nicety. Revised table:

| Failure | SQS outcome | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| `queryGsi3Page` transient DynamoDB error | `batchItemFailures` (retried) | unchanged from round 2 |
| Malformed scan-continuation payload (schema-invalid) | `batchItemFailures` (retried up to `maxReceiveCount`) + `ScanMessageValidationFailure` metric/alarm at >0 | round 2's "log-only" reversed Ã¢â‚¬â€ Codex correctly flagged silent work-unit loss risk; retrying doesn't help a truly malformed message, but it DOES give the alarm time to page before the DLQ absorbs it after 5 tries, and a message that's malformed due to a transient serialization bug (not impossible) gets a chance to succeed on a redeploy before exhausting retries |
| Lease acquire conditional check failed | ack'd, no-op, `LeaseAcquireOutcome{contended}` | unchanged |
| Lease reclaim succeeds | ack'd, `LeaseAcquireOutcome{reclaimed}` | **this IS required change 10's stalled-chain signal Ã¢â‚¬â€ see below** |
| Checkpoint conditional check failed (stale/duplicate continuation) | ack'd, no-op | unchanged reasoning, now safe by construction (Ã‚Â§1-2) |
| `SendMessageBatch` sender-fault entry | invocation throws, `CandidateSenderFault` metric+alarm | reversed per Ã‚Â§5 |
| Claim consumer `transactWrite` cancelled, occurrence-update entry's reason via `getCancellationReasonCodes` = `ConditionalCheckFailed` | ack'd, no-op (`lost-race`) | the ONLY case that's a true lost race Ã¢â‚¬â€ fixed per Codex's finding |
| Claim consumer `transactWrite` cancelled, any OTHER reason (including on the outbox Put entry) | `batchItemFailures` (retried) | genuine transient failure, now correctly distinguished instead of collapsed |
| Unknown GSI3 discriminator | **invocation throws** (restores `shouldAlarm()`'s existing fail-closed behavior, `producer.ts:149-156`) | round 2 wrongly softened this to a no-op; reversed Ã¢â‚¬â€ D-039's fail-closed intent is preserved unchanged, not weakened by this redesign |

## Required change 8/10: stalled-chain detection Ã¢â‚¬â€ reuses `LeaseAcquireOutcome{reclaimed}`, no new query

No separate periodic reconciliation query is needed: because Ã‚Â§3's enumeration re-evaluates the
FULL lookback window (15 minutes) on EVERY tick (unchanged from today), any lease that goes stale

## Required change 13Ã¢â€ â€™ this round's Ã‚Â§: deploy/rollback via explicit env-var toggle

Codex's own three suggested options include "a temporary handler-routing/feature switch" Ã¢â‚¬â€ this
plan adopts it explicitly, addressing the earlier concern that D-299 "rejected a flag": D-299
rejected PERMANENTLY running old and new claim logic concurrently against the same table (a
correctness/race concern Ã¢â‚¬â€ doubling the concurrent-claim surface indefinitely). A **deploy-time-only
env var** (`SCAN_MODE: "LEGACY" | "PAGED"`, read once at cold start, no per-invocation branching
risk) is a materially different, lesser thing: at any given moment exactly ONE mode is live (never
both), and the var is deleted entirely (code for `"LEGACY"` removed) in the third, later change Ã¢â‚¬â€
it is a rollout mechanism with a defined end, not a standing dual-path architecture.
- **Apply 1**: claim queue + consumer (event-source-mapping enabled, inert Ã¢â‚¬â€ nothing publishes to
  it), scan queue (event-source-mapping enabled Ã¢â‚¬â€ also inert, nothing publishes to it either, since
  `SCAN_MODE=LEGACY` never emits start messages), new port/adapter/handler code deployed but
  `SCAN_MODE=LEGACY` at the environment level keeps `reminder-producer-handler.ts` executing
  exactly today's `runProducerTick` path. This IS enough to make Apply 1 genuinely inert (Codex's
  exact objection to round 2), because the toggle lives in application code reading `process.env`,
  not in Terraform resource wiring whose ordering Terraform doesn't guarantee.
- **Apply 2**: flips `SCAN_MODE=PAGED` via a Lambda environment variable update Ã¢â‚¬â€ a single
  Terraform-managed attribute change, applied atomically to the function configuration (no
  cross-resource ordering concern, since it's one resource's one attribute).
- **Lease/queue cleanup on rollback**: revert Apply 2's env var back to `LEGACY`. In-flight scan
  chains stop producing new checkpoints (no consumer reads them meaningfully once `LEGACY` code
  ignores SQS-sourced invocations Ã¢â‚¬â€ the SQS-triggered handler branch checks `SCAN_MODE` too and
  no-ops with a log line if rolled back mid-flight, rather than assuming it's never invoked).
  Abandoned lease rows expire via `purgeAfterTtl` (corrected attribute name,
  `infra/modules/dynamo-table/main.tf:206-208` Ã¢â‚¬â€ round 2's `ttl` typo fixed) at `leaseUntil + 7d`,
  unchanged from round 1/2's retention choice. Queued-but-unprocessed scan/claim messages age out
  via each queue's normal 4-day retention or get DLQ'd after `maxReceiveCount=5` Ã¢â‚¬â€ both bounded,
  self-cleaning, no manual drain step required, though a runbook note (not a blocking step) to
  purge the claim queue manually before an unusually long rollback window is worth adding in the
  final artifact.

296:12:## Research declaration (research-protocol.md, E-014)
297:13:
298:14:**SIM PARCIAL.** The macro-pattern (decouple scan from claim via two queues) is already
299:15:externally researched and cited in D-299 (AWS Prescriptive Guidance, Lambda+SQS developer guide,
300:16:SQS API reference). What's new at THIS level is a sub-decision AWS has a well-documented but
301:17:non-obvious answer for: **SQS visibility timeout sizing relative to Lambda timeout, and its
302:18:interaction with `maxReceiveCount`/DLQ redelivery for a handler that holds an idempotency lease**.
303:19:This project's own `sqs-worker-queue` module already encodes one specific answer (6x, fixed,
304:20:`maxReceiveCount=5`) as a blanket rule for the dispatch case ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â applying it unmodified to a
305:21:lease-holding consumer needs to be checked against AWS's own guidance on visibility timeout vs.
306:22:in-flight processing time, because a lease-based state machine changes what "redelivery mid-lease"
307:23:means (D-299's own R3ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â€žÂ¢R4 finding). Checklist applied this round, sourced from AWS Lambda Developer
308:24:Guide "Using Lambda with Amazon SQS" (event source mapping / partial batch response) and AWS SQS
309:25:"Amazon SQS visibility timeout" page (both already cited as sources in D-299, re-read here for the
310:26:consumer-timeout-vs-lease-duration angle specifically, no new source needed):
311:27:1. Visibility timeout must exceed **worst-case** processing time, not average ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â for a lease-based
312:28:   consumer, worst case includes lease renewal, not just one page's work.
313:29:2. `maxReceiveCount` ÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â avg processing time bounds how long a poison message cycles before DLQ ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â
314:30:   must be reconciled with lease `leaseUntil` duration so an expired lease and an SQS redelivery
315:31:   don't race in a way that duplicates or drops work (D-299's exact concern, now at the queue-timer
316:32:   level instead of the state-machine level).
317:33:3. Batch size for the scan-continuation queue must stay effectively 1 (see ÃƒÆ’Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§3 below) ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â AWS's own
318:34:   guidance warns partial-batch-failure handling gets materially harder above batch size 1 when
319:35:   messages are causally chained (continuation N+1 must not be visible before N's page commits).

355:71:## 2. Page-lease state machine
356:72:
357:73:**Item** (main table, single-table design ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â PK/SK pattern matches existing shard-scan items in
358:74:`dynamodb-reminder-producer-store.ts`, confirmed against that file):
359:75:
360:76:```
361:77:PK: SCAN#<shardId>#<tickMinuteISO>     e.g. SCAN#3#2026-09-14T22:31:00Z
362:78:SK: LEASE
363:79:entityType: "ReminderScanLease"
364:80:status: "IN_PROGRESS" | "COMPLETED"
365:81:ownerToken: string (randomUUID, one per Lambda invocation attempt ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â NOT per SQS messageId,
366:82:            so a redelivered SQS message that re-enters the same invocation semantics gets a
367:83:            fresh token and must re-win the conditional acquire, closing the exact silent-drop
368:84:            hole D-299 R3 found in the stateless-fence design)
369:85:leaseUntil: number (epoch ms)
370:86:lastEvaluatedKey: string | undefined (JSON-serialized DynamoDB ExclusiveStartKey for queryGsi3,
371:87:            undefined on the first page, present on every continuation)
372:88:pagesProcessed: number
373:89:candidatesPublished: number
374:90:version: number (occ.ts optimistic concurrency, same convention as every other mutable item)
375:91:ttl: epoch seconds, 7 days after leaseUntil ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â cheap cleanup, matches this project's existing TTL
376:92:     convention on other transient coordination items (checked against `defaultShardConfig()`'s
377:93:     neighbors in dynamodb-reminder-producer-store.ts)
378:94:```
379:95:
380:96:**Acquire** (first page of a shard/minute, or reclaim after expiry) ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â `occ.ts`'s
381:97:`buildConditionalPut` with:
382:98:`ConditionExpression: "attribute_not_exists(PK) OR (status = :inProgress AND leaseUntil < :now) OR status = :completedNoop"`
383:99:ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â the third arm exists only to make a duplicate "start" message (a Scheduler retry firing the same
384:100:shard/minute twice) a safe no-op rather than an error; it still writes nothing new when already
385:101:`COMPLETED` (checked in application code before the Put, not relied on as a silent race ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â same
386:102:"belt AND suspenders" pattern `runProducerTick` already uses for claim races today).
387:103:
388:104:**Renew** (before publishing each continuation) ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â `occ.ts`'s `buildVersionedUpdate` with
389:105:`ConditionExpression: "ownerToken = :myToken AND version = :expectedVersion"`: sets new
390:106:`leaseUntil`, `lastEvaluatedKey`, increments `pagesProcessed`/`candidatesPublished`, bumps
391:107:`version`. **This update happens AFTER the claim-queue `SendMessageBatch` succeeds and BEFORE the
392:108:continuation message is sent** ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â ordering matters: if the process dies between the batch send and
393:109:the lease renew, the next attempt (a fresh SQS redelivery of the SAME scan message, since it never
394:110:completed) re-reads `lastEvaluatedKey` from the STALE lease state (pre-this-page), re-queries the
395:111:same page from `queryGsi3` (deterministic per `lastEvaluatedKey`), and re-publishes the same
396:112:candidates. This is why **claim-queue candidates must be idempotent to redelivery independent of
397:113:this lease** ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â already true by construction, because the claim consumer's own conditional
398:114:`transactWrite` (ÃƒÆ’Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§ below) is the actual idempotency boundary for claiming, not the scan side. The
399:115:lease's job is only to make forward SCAN progress resumable exactly-once-effectively, not to
400:116:dedupe claims (that guarantee already exists one layer down).
401:117:
402:118:**Release** (last page, `queryGsi3` returns no `LastEvaluatedKey`) ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â `buildVersionedUpdate` sets
403:119:`status = "COMPLETED"`, same ownerToken/version condition.
404:120:
405:121:**Expire**: no active "expire" write ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â a lease simply becomes reclaimable once `leaseUntil < now`,
406:122:matched by the Acquire condition above. No separate reconciliation pass is added for this (see ÃƒÆ’Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§6
407:123:ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â `reminder-reconciliation.ts` is untouched; lease reclaim is self-contained inside the scan path,
408:124:triggered by the SAME continuation message that would have fired next, since EventBridge Scheduler
409:125:fires a new tick every minute and a new tick for an ALREADY in-progress shard is the natural
410:126:reclaim trigger ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â see ÃƒÆ’Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§7 for why this is safe rather than racy).

412:128:## 3. Timeout/visibility sizing
413:129:
414:130:Fixed module facts (not renegotiable without a `sqs-worker-queue` module change, out of scope
415:131:here): `visibility_timeout_seconds = consumer_timeout_seconds * 6`, `maxReceiveCount = 5` fixed.
416:132:
417:133:- **Scan Lambda timeout**: 30s (one `queryGsi3` page + one `SendMessageBatch` + one lease
418:134:  renew/acquire ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â bounded work, generous margin over p99). ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â€žÂ¢ scan queue visibility timeout = 180s
419:135:  (module-derived, 6x).
420:136:- **Claim Lambda timeout**: 10s (unchanged from today's per-occurrence claim ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â a single `get` +
421:137:  `transactWrite`, same cost as today's inner loop iteration). ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â€žÂ¢ claim queue visibility timeout =
422:138:  60s (module-derived, 6x).
423:139:- **Lease duration** (`leaseUntil - leaseAcquiredAt`): **90s** ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â set independently of the Lambda
424:140:  timeout (it is a business-level mutual-exclusion window, not a retry mechanism) but sized against
425:141:  it with an explicit invariant: **lease duration ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â°Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â¥ 2x scan Lambda timeout** (30sÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â2=60s ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â°Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â¤ 90s),
426:142:  giving one full retry's worth of headroom before a DIFFERENT invocation is allowed to steal the
427:143:  lease, so a slow-but-alive attempt is never pre-empted by its own SQS-triggered retry racing in.
428:144:  Combined with **scan visibility timeout (180s) > lease duration (90s)**, an SQS redelivery of the
429:145:  SAME message can never arrive before the lease it would contend with has already legitimately
430:146:  expired ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â removing the specific race D-299 R3 found (two live workers believing they both hold
431:147:  the lease) by construction, not by luck.
432:148:- **`maxReceiveCount=5` (fixed)** on the scan queue means a poison continuation message cycles for
433:149:  up to 5ÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â180s = 900s (15 min) before DLQ ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â acceptable, since EventBridge Scheduler fires a new
434:150:  tick every 60s regardless, so a stuck shard's lease will be reclaimed by a FRESH tick's message
435:151:  well before the poison copy DLQs; the DLQ path exists for the case where `queryGsi3` itself is
436:152:  erroring (data/query bug), not for ordinary transient contention.
437:153:- **Batch size**: scan queue consumer batch size = **1** (continuation messages are causally
438:154:  chained per shard ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â processing two "next page" messages for the same shard concurrently is
439:155:  exactly the race this design eliminates via the lease, so the event-source-mapping must not
440:156:  create that race by delivering >1 at once). Claim queue consumer batch size = **10** (candidates
441:157:  are independent per occurrence, matches `reminder-dispatch`'s existing batch size ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â confirmed
442:158:  against `infra/main.tf`'s `reminder_dispatch_from_queue` event source mapping).
443:159:- **Concurrency invariant** (D-299, now with numbers): scan queue
444:160:  `reserved_concurrent_executions` = number of shards (`defaultShardConfig()`'s shard count,
445:161:  confirmed = `DEFAULT_SHARD_COUNT = 4` in `src/modules/reminder/domain/shard-config.ts`) ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â one in-flight scan per shard by
446:162:  construction (the lease already enforces this logically; the Lambda concurrency cap is defense in
447:163:  depth, cheap to set). Claim queue `reserved_concurrent_executions` = **16** (ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â°Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â¥ sum of scan's
448:164:  per-page candidate fan-out ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â a page of `queryGsi3` batches up to 25 candidates per
449:165:  `SendMessageBatch` call, ÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â4 shards worst-case-concurrent = 100 theoretical peak sends, but claim
450:166:  Lambda p50 is <200ms so 16 concurrent claim workers clears a 100-item burst in ~1.3s ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â matches
451:167:  PERF-12's own 10k-in-a-minute volume target with margin, verified against PERF-12's report
452:168:  numbers in `docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-structural-fix-scoping/` round artifacts).

454:170:## 4. Tracing/logging/metrics/errors/outbox/writes ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â concrete
455:171:
456:172:- **Correlation ID propagation**: the ORIGINAL scan tick's `randomUUID()` (today's

488:204:    duplicating).

492:208:  unchanged AppError subclasses for downstream failures ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â no new subclass needed, confirmed by
493:209:  reading the union in `app-error.ts`; if a future round finds a gap, add
494:210:  `ReminderLeaseConflictError extends AppError` only if contention needs to surface as a retryable
495:211:  error rather than a logged no-op ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â deferred as a round-2 open question, not assumed here).
496:212:- **Outbox**: candidates and the continuation message are **NOT** written via the transactional
497:213:  outbox pattern, and this is a deliberate deviation from AGENTS.md's "critical side-effect in the
498:214:  same transaction as the aggregate write" rule ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â because there IS no aggregate write at scan time
499:215:  (the scan step only reads GSI3 and writes its OWN lease item; the occurrence aggregate write only
500:216:  happens later, in the claim consumer). The outbox pattern's applicability is at the CLAIM step:
501:217:  the claim consumer's existing `get`+`transactWrite` (unchanged from today) is the aggregate
502:218:  write, and it already should (today's code should be checked, not assumed ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â round 2 action item)
503:219:  carry its resulting event via the SAME `TransactWriteItems`, exactly like `SQS_REMINDER_DISPATCH_V1`
504:220:  today. Round 1 conclusion: **outbox governs the claimÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â€žÂ¢dispatch boundary (unchanged from today),
505:221:  not the scanÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â€žÂ¢claim boundary (new, and necessarily a direct `SendMessageBatch`, not outbox-mediated,
506:222:  because outbox requires a DynamoDB transaction and the scan step's transaction is the lease
507:223:  write, which is unrelated to the individual candidates being published)**.
508:224:- **DynamoDB writes**: lease acquire/renew/release exclusively via `occ.ts`'s
509:225:  `buildConditionalPut`/`buildVersionedUpdate` (no raw `PutItem`/`UpdateItem`), confirmed pattern
510:226:  match against existing shard-scan-state usage in `dynamodb-reminder-producer-store.ts`.
511:227:

535:251:## 6. `reminder-reconciliation.ts` impact
536:252:
537:253:**Confirmed: no change needed**, with actual reasoning (not just repeating D-299's stated
538:254:expectation): `reminder-reconciliation.ts`'s job (per its own file, to be re-read in round 2 for a
539:255:citation-level confirmation) is to catch occurrences stuck in `CLAIMED` past `claimExpiresAt` ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â
540:256:that contract is entirely downstream of the claim consumer's `transactWrite`, which writes
541:257:`claimExpiresAt` identically to today's code (D-299's own premise, unchanged by this plan since the
542:258:claim logic itself is only relocated, not rewritten). The scan-side lease this plan adds is a
543:259:DIFFERENT state machine on a DIFFERENT item (`SCAN#...#LEASE`, never `CLAIMED` occurrence rows) that
544:260:reconciliation never reads today and has no reason to start reading ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â a stuck scan lease
545:261:self-heals via the next EventBridge tick's reclaim path (ÃƒÆ’Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§2), not via reconciliation. One residual
546:262:open question for round 2: does reconciliation's own scan of `CLAIMED` rows need its OWN
547:263:correlation ID propagation update for consistency, even though its logic doesn't change? (Leaning
548:264:no ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â it's not part of this mechanism's message chain ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â but flagging rather than asserting.)
549:265:
550:266:## 7. Migration/rollout
551:267:
552:268:Big-bang cutover, not staged, for a concrete reason: the scan and claim halves are not
553:269:independently useful (a scan queue with no claim consumer just accumulates candidates; a claim
554:270:consumer with no new-shape scan producer never receives anything) ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â there's no safe intermediate
555:271:state to stage through, unlike, say, a dual-write migration. Sequencing:
556:272:1. Deploy claim consumer Lambda + claim queue (inert ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â nothing publishes to it yet).
557:273:2. Deploy scan queue (inert ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â nothing subscribes to the OLD producer's shard-loop yet, since it
558:274:   doesn't publish to it).
559:275:3. Deploy the MODIFIED `reminder-producer-handler.ts` (now page-based) in the SAME release as step
560:276:   1/2's infra ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â this is the actual cutover moment; the old monolithic-per-shard loop code path is
561:277:   deleted in this same change, not kept behind a flag (D-299 didn't ask for a flag, and a flag
562:278:   here would mean maintaining two claim code paths against the same table, doubling the
563:279:   concurrent-claim race surface this whole fix targets).
564:280:4. **Occurrences already `SCHEDULED` at cutover**: confirmed safe, with reasoning ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â `SCHEDULED`
565:281:   occurrences are discovered by `queryGsi3`, not by any in-flight queue state; the OLD mechanism's
566:282:   only in-flight artifact at cutover is whatever's already sitting in the OLD single-invocation
567:283:   claim loop of a tick that started before deploy (which either finishes normally before the
568:284:   deploy completes, since Lambda in-flight invocations aren't killed by a code update, or times
569:285:   out and is picked up fresh by the NEW scan mechanism's next tick ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â no occurrence-level state is
570:286:   lost either way, since `SCHEDULED` occurrences are read fresh from GSI3 every tick regardless of
571:287:   which mechanism is running).
572:288:5. Rollback path: revert step 3's Lambda code only (keep the new queues/consumer deployed but
573:289:   inert) ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â since GSI3 access never moved, a revert to the old handler code resumes the old
574:290:   monolithic scan immediately with no data migration needed in either direction.

1299:710:# D-233: SEC-R2-02 fix. Two changes from the original mapping:
1300:711:#  - filter_criteria now also matches on entityType - the marker's OWN Put/Update/Delete writes
1301:712:#    (D-233's new claim/lease mechanism) already generate stream INSERT/MODIFY events on this
1302:713:#    same table; without this filter they'd reach the handler, get classified "malformed" by
1303:714:#    isDeliveryRecord(), and inflate batchItemFailures/the failure queue with pure noise (a latent
1304:715:#    bug that predates D-233 too, since claim()'s original PutItem already wrote a marker row).
1305:716:#  - maximum_retry_attempts/maximum_record_age_in_seconds set to -1 (unlimited, bounded only by
1306:717:#    DynamoDB Streams' own native 24h retention) - a bounded retry count/age (the previous
1307:718:#    3/3600) could exhaust BEFORE the marker's 30s claim lease ever expires, leaving
1308:719:#    SKIPPED_LEASE_ACTIVE retries stuck with no path to the SEND_UNCERTAIN reconciliation
1309:720:#    deliver.ts relies on. The IteratorAge alarm below is the real backstop for a genuinely
1310:721:#    stuck/poison record - it fires in minutes, not after the 24h native retention discards it.

2381:1792:# --- UploadFinalizerWorker: S3 event (via queue) -> validate + invoke ParserSandbox ---------
2382:1793:
2383:1794:# Real bug found via Camada 3 (2026-08-22): UploadFinalizerWorker only had READ access to the
2384:1795:# quarantine bucket, but advanceAfterEvidence() (called identically by both workers) performs
2385:1796:# the actual quarantine->clean promotion copy whichever worker's evidence completes the pair
2386:1797:# LAST - which is not always MalwareResultWorker. A real upload where the finalizer's own
2387:1798:# evidence-persist step landed after the malware scan result hit exactly this: the finalizer
2388:1799:# won the PROMOTE race and got a real AccessDenied trying s3:PutObject on the clean bucket.
2389:1800:# Both workers need IDENTICAL object-access permissions for this reason - kept as two
2390:1801:# separately-named data sources (not a single shared one) so each function's IAM role
2391:1802:# document stays self-explanatory in `aws iam` output, but the statements are deliberately
2392:1803:# identical to malware_result_object_access below.
2393:1804:data "aws_iam_policy_document" "upload_finalizer_object_access" {
2394:1805:  statement {
2395:1806:    sid       = "ReadDeleteQuarantineObjects"
2396:1807:    effect    = "Allow"
2397:1808:    actions   = ["s3:GetObject", "s3:GetObjectVersion", "s3:DeleteObjectVersion"]
2398:1809:    resources = ["${module.document_buckets.quarantine_bucket_arn}/*"]
2399:1810:  }
2400:1811:  statement {
2401:1812:    # Real bug found via Camada 3 (2026-08-22): advanceAfterEvidence() calls headObject() on
2402:1813:    # the clean bucket right after copyObject() to VERIFY the promotion copy actually landed
2403:1814:    # before confirming CLEAN - S3's HeadObject API requires the s3:GetObject IAM action (a
2404:1815:    # well-known S3 quirk: there is no separate "HeadObject" IAM action), which was never
2405:1816:    # granted here (only PutObject was). The copy itself succeeded every time; only the
2406:1817:    # verification step 403'd, surfaced by the AWS SDK as an opaque "UnknownError" rather than
2407:1818:    # a clean AccessDenied.
2408:1819:    sid       = "ReadWriteCleanObjects"
2409:1820:    effect    = "Allow"
2410:1821:    actions   = ["s3:GetObject", "s3:GetObjectVersion", "s3:PutObject"]
2411:1822:    resources = ["${module.document_buckets.clean_bucket_arn}/*"]
2412:1823:  }
2413:1824:  statement {
2414:1825:    sid       = "DecryptQuarantineObjects"
2415:1826:    effect    = "Allow"
2416:1827:    actions   = ["kms:Decrypt"]
2417:1828:    resources = [module.document_buckets.quarantine_kms_key_arn]

5402:1:/**
5403:2: * Request-scoped correlation context via AsyncLocalStorage (m5-observability-design.md #2).
5404:3: * runWithContext is called once per record for batch handlers (SQS, DynamoDB Streams, sweeper) -
5405:4: * never once per invocation for those - so context never leaks across records in the same batch.
5406:5: */
5407:6:import { AsyncLocalStorage } from "node:async_hooks";
5408:7:
5409:8:export interface RequestContext {
5410:9:  correlationId: string;
5411:10:  tenantId?: string;
5412:11:  requestId?: string;
5413:12:}
5414:13:
5415:14:const storage = new AsyncLocalStorage<RequestContext>();
5416:15:
5417:16:export function runWithContext<T>(context: RequestContext, fn: () => T): T {
5418:17:  return storage.run(context, fn);
5419:18:}
5420:19:
5421:20:export function getContext(): RequestContext | undefined {
5422:21:  return storage.getStore();
5423:22:}

5426:25: * m5-observability-design.md #2: correlationId for an SQS record whose sender (relay/

5428:27: * original business correlationId via this exact MessageAttribute name - see
5429:28: * outboxRecordCorrelationId (src/shared/outbox/outbox.ts) for the sender side of this same
5430:29: * contract. Falls back to the SQS messageId only for a message that never got the
5431:30: * attribute (pre-M5 in-flight, or a queue whose producer has no upstream correlationId to
5432:31: * propagate, e.g. SES/SNS-sourced messages) - pulled out as its own pure function so the

5478:39:  const dimensionNames = Object.keys(point.dimensions ?? {});

5497:58: * handler calling it, same discipline `SecureLogger` already follows for logging itself.
5498:59: * `namespace` groups metrics in the CloudWatch console (e.g. `"ExpirationTracker/ReminderDispatch"`).

5575:66:  expectedVersion: number;
5576:67:  set: Record<string, unknown>;
5577:68:  remove?: string[];
5578:69:  now?: string;
5579:70:  extraConditions?: Array<{ expression: string; names?: Record<string, string>; values?: Record<string, unknown> }>;
5580:71:}
5581:72:
5582:73:/**
5583:74: * Private core shared by `buildVersionedUpdate()` (tenant-fenced, every ordinary business
5584:75: * entity) and `buildAccountScopedVersionedUpdate()` (D-197 fatia 3/5: WhatsApp `WebhookInbox`,
5585:76: * the first entity in this repo with no tenant at all - see
5586:77: * `docs/architecture/reviews/whatsapp-channel-scoping/webhook-inbox-purge-scoping/` for the
5587:78: * 3-round Claude<->Codex protocol, both final notes >=9.0, that decided this shape). The ONLY
5588:79: * difference between the two public builders is which attribute anchors the scope fence
5589:80: * (`tenantId` vs `accountId`) - version increment, `updatedAt`, SET/REMOVE generation,
5590:81: * `extraConditions` composition and placeholder-collision detection are a single implementation,
5591:82: * never duplicated, so the two builders can never drift apart on anything but their fence.
5592:83: */
5593:84:function buildScopedVersionedUpdate(input: ScopedVersionedUpdateInput, scope: ScopeCondition): DynamoUpdateCommandInput {
5594:85:  const now = input.now ?? new Date().toISOString();
5595:86:
5596:87:  const names: Record<string, string> = {
5597:88:    "#version": "version",
5598:89:    [scope.namePlaceholder]: scope.attributeName,
5599:90:    "#updatedAt": "updatedAt",
5600:91:  };
5601:92:  const values: Record<string, unknown> = {
5602:93:    ":expectedVersion": input.expectedVersion,
5603:94:    [scope.valuePlaceholder]: scope.value,
5604:95:    ":one": 1,
5605:96:    ":now": now,
5606:97:  };
5607:98:
5608:99:  const setClauses = ["#version = #version + :one", "#updatedAt = :now"];
5609:100:  let i = 0;
5610:101:  for (const [field, value] of Object.entries(input.set)) {
5611:102:    const nameKey = `#set${i}`;
5612:103:    const valueKey = `:set${i}`;
5613:104:    names[nameKey] = field;
5614:105:    values[valueKey] = value;
5615:106:    setClauses.push(`${nameKey} = ${valueKey}`);
5616:107:    i += 1;
5617:108:  }
5618:109:
5619:110:  const removeClauses: string[] = [];
5620:111:  let j = 0;
5621:112:  for (const field of input.remove ?? []) {
5622:113:    const nameKey = `#rem${j}`;
5623:114:    names[nameKey] = field;
5624:115:    removeClauses.push(nameKey);
5625:116:    j += 1;
5626:117:  }
5627:118:
5628:119:  const expression =
5629:120:    removeClauses.length > 0
5630:121:      ? `SET ${setClauses.join(", ")} REMOVE ${removeClauses.join(", ")}`
5631:122:      : `SET ${setClauses.join(", ")}`;
5632:123:
5633:124:  const baseConditionParts = ["attribute_exists(PK)", "attribute_exists(SK)", "#version = :expectedVersion", `${scope.namePlaceholder} = ${scope.valuePlaceholder}`];
5634:125:  for (const extra of input.extraConditions ?? []) {
5635:126:    for (const [nameKey, name] of Object.entries(extra.names ?? {})) {
5636:127:      if (nameKey in names) throw new Error(`extraConditions name placeholder collides with a reserved/generated key: ${nameKey}`);
5637:128:      names[nameKey] = name;
5638:129:    }
5639:130:    for (const [valueKey, value] of Object.entries(extra.values ?? {})) {
5640:131:      if (valueKey in values) throw new Error(`extraConditions value placeholder collides with a reserved/generated key: ${valueKey}`);
5641:132:      values[valueKey] = value;
5642:133:    }
5643:134:    baseConditionParts.push(`(${extra.expression})`);
5644:135:  }
5645:136:
5646:137:  return {
5647:138:    TableName: input.tableName,
5648:139:    Key: input.key,
5649:140:    UpdateExpression: expression,
5650:141:    ConditionExpression: baseConditionParts.join(" AND "),
5651:142:    ExpressionAttributeNames: names,
5652:143:    ExpressionAttributeValues: values,
5653:144:  };
5654:145:}
5655:146:
5656:147:/**
5657:148: * Builds an UpdateItem input enforcing implementation-blueprint.md #5.2's exact
5658:149: * ConditionExpression: attribute_exists(PK) AND attribute_exists(SK) AND
5659:150: * #version = :expectedVersion AND #tenantId = :tenantId, and increments version atomically.
5660:151: * Contractually unchanged by the account-scoped sibling below - same signature, same generated
5661:152: * expression, byte-for-byte, for every one of this repo's ~40 existing call sites.
5662:153: */
5663:154:export function buildVersionedUpdate(input: VersionedUpdateInput): DynamoUpdateCommandInput {
5664:155:  return buildScopedVersionedUpdate(input, { namePlaceholder: "#tenantId", attributeName: "tenantId", valuePlaceholder: ":tenantId", value: input.tenantId });
5665:156:}

6314:123:/**
6315:124: * PERF-12 1k load test finding (docs/engineering/performance/results/PERF-12-async-pipeline-1k.md):
6316:125: * this loop used to process one occurrence at a time - one `store.get` + one
6317:126: * `store.transactWrite` per occurrence, fully sequential - inside a Lambda with (at the time)
6318:127: * a 10s timeout. With ~250 occurrences concentrated in one shard/minute under a realistic
6319:128: * burst, that budget was nowhere near enough, the function was killed mid-loop repeatedly, and
6320:129: * occurrences that hadn't been claimed yet eventually aged out of the lookback window,
6321:130: * permanently stuck in SCHEDULED. Bounded concurrency here mirrors the exact pattern already
6322:131: * used for the same reason in reminder-dispatch-handler.ts (D-170) - each occurrence's own
6323:132: * `transactWrite` stays a single, independent atomic conditional claim (never merged across
6324:133: * occurrences), so parallelizing here does not touch the transactional or idempotency
6325:134: * guarantees of any individual claim, only how many claims run concurrently. A plain numeric
6326:135: * constant, not unbounded `Promise.all`, to keep the burst of concurrent DynamoDB round trips
6327:136: * per invocation predictable.
6328:137: */
6329:138:const PRODUCER_CLAIM_CONCURRENCY = 8;
6330:139:
6331:140:/**
6332:141: * Pure alarm decision, extracted so the Lambda handler's "when should this tick throw" logic
6333:142: * is unit-testable without mocking the whole handler/composition root (achado real de revisÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â£o
6334:143: * adversarial, D-039/D-046/D-048: an earlier version of this fail-closed path was silently
6335:144: * absorbed by the handler - `unknownEntityType` was counted but nothing ever read it). Two
6336:145: * independent reasons, checked in this order for a stable, deterministic message:
6337:146: * unrecognized GSI3SK shape (fail-closed, never a retry-race) first, then genuine per-occurrence
6338:147: * claim failures.
6339:148: */
6340:149:export function shouldAlarm(result: ProducerTickResult): { alarm: boolean; reason?: string } {
6341:150:  if (result.unknownEntityType > 0) {
6342:151:    return { alarm: true, reason: `reminder-producer: ${result.unknownEntityType} GSI3 row(s) matched neither the reminder nor the chasing entityType - fail-closed` };
6343:152:  }
6344:153:  if (result.failed.length > 0) {
6345:154:    return { alarm: true, reason: `reminder-producer: ${result.failed.length} occurrence(s) failed to claim` };
6346:155:  }
6347:156:  return { alarm: false };
6348:157:}

6350:159:/** Runs one producer tick for wall-clock minute `tickMinute` (already floored to the minute by the caller/Lambda trigger). */
6351:160:export async function runProducerTick(deps: ProducerDeps, tickMinute: Date): Promise<ProducerTickResult> {
6352:161:  const generations = activeGenerations(deps.shardConfig, deps.now());
6353:162:  const lookback = deps.lookbackMinutes ?? 15;
6354:163:  const claimTtlMs = deps.claimTtlMs ?? 2 * 60_000;
6355:164:
6356:165:  const minutesToScan: Date[] = [];
6357:166:  for (let i = lookback; i >= 0; i--) {
6358:167:    minutesToScan.push(minuteFloor(new Date(tickMinute.getTime() - i * 60_000)));
6359:168:  }
6360:169:

6362:171:  const chasingClaimed: ChasingDispatchCommand[] = [];

6364:173:  let unknownEntityType = 0;
6365:174:  let scanned = 0;
6366:175:  let partitions = 0;
6367:176:
6368:177:  // Dedup guard: the same occurrence could show up in more than one scanned minute only if
6369:178:  // materialization ever wrote it under a stale bucket, which shouldn't happen - but a
6370:179:  // Set guards against double-claiming within a single tick regardless.
6371:180:  const seen = new Set<string>();

6376:185:      partitions += partitionKeys.length;

6379:188:        // PERF-12: this used to be `for (const row of rows)`, one `get`+`transactWrite` pair
6380:189:        // processed strictly sequentially - see PRODUCER_CLAIM_CONCURRENCY's doc comment for
6381:190:        // why bounded concurrency replaces that here. `seen`/`claimed`/`failed`/
6382:191:        // `chasingClaimed`/counters are shared mutable state across concurrent callbacks, but
6383:192:        // every access happens either synchronously (no `await` in between, so the JS event
6384:193:        // loop cannot interleave two callbacks' synchronous sections) or as an atomic
6385:194:        // push/increment - never a race in practice under Node's single-threaded model.

6392:201:          if (chasingParsed) {

6394:203:            seen.add(chasingParsed.occurrenceId);
6395:204:            try {
6396:205:              const outcome = await claimChasingOccurrence(

6646:62:async function handleReconciliation(event: ReminderReconciliationEvent): Promise<void> {
6647:63:  const mode = event.mode;
6648:64:
6649:65:  const expiredClaimCandidates: ReminderOccurrence[] = [];
6650:66:  const dstCandidates: FullDstCandidate[] = [];
6651:67:
6652:68:  if (mode === "CLAIMS") {
6653:69:    // GSI6 is ALL-projected - each candidate row already IS the full ReminderOccurrence
6654:70:    // item (see ExpiredClaimCandidate's doc comment), so no extra fetch is needed.
6655:71:    // Pagination is drained (bug found by Codex implementation review: the first version
6656:72:    // only ever read page 1, silently leaving any backlog over one page unprocessed).
6657:73:    let cursor: string | undefined;
6658:74:    for (let page = 0; page < MAX_PAGES; page++) {
6659:75:      const result = await candidateSource.listExpiredClaims({ before: now(), cursor });
6660:76:      expiredClaimCandidates.push(...(result.items as unknown as ReminderOccurrence[]));
6661:77:      if (!result.cursor) break;
6662:78:      cursor = result.cursor;
6663:79:    }
6664:80:  }
6665:81:
6666:82:  if (mode === "DST") {
6667:83:    // ReminderMaterializer (M3.5) writes a WORKSTATE#DST_PENDING GSI6 pointer whenever a
6668:84:    // trigger's schedule was computed at an ambiguous/nonexistent local time, OR whose
6669:85:    // timeZone observes DST at all (see reminder-materializer.ts - broadened per Codex
6670:86:    // implementation review: a non-ambiguous 09:00 reminder in a DST-observing zone can
6671:87:    // still need re-evaluation after an offset change, not just literally-ambiguous ones).
6672:88:    // This query finds those candidates; occurrences in a fixed-offset timeZone never
6673:89:    // appear here at all.
6674:90:    const windowStart = now();
6675:91:    const windowEnd = new Date(Date.parse(windowStart) + 7 * 24 * 60 * 60_000).toISOString();
6676:92:    let cursor: string | undefined;
6677:93:    for (let page = 0; page < MAX_PAGES; page++) {
6678:94:      const result = await candidateSource.listDstCandidates({ window: { start: windowStart, end: windowEnd }, cursor });
6679:95:      for (const light of result.items) {
6680:96:        const policy = await store.get<ReminderPolicy>(policyKey(light.tenantId, light.policyId));
6681:97:        if (!policy) continue;
6682:98:        const item = await store.get<{ PK: string; SK: string; dueDate: string; version: number }>(itemKey(authorizedTenantIdFromPersistedEntity(light), light.itemId));
6683:99:        if (!item) continue;
6684:100:        dstCandidates.push({
6685:101:          tenantId: light.tenantId,
6686:102:          itemId: light.itemId,
6687:103:          itemVersion: item.version,
6688:104:          itemDueDate: item.dueDate,
6689:105:          policy,
6690:106:        });
6691:107:      }
6692:108:      if (!result.cursor) break;
6693:109:      cursor = result.cursor;
6694:110:    }
6695:111:  }
6696:112:
6697:113:  const result = await runReconciliation({ store, tableName, now, shardConfig }, { expiredClaimCandidates, dstCandidates });
6698:114:  logger.info("reminder-reconciliation complete", { mode, scheduledTime: event.scheduledTime, ...result });

6703:3: * doubling N cannot make occurrences already materialized under the OLD generation
6704:4: * invisible. `shardFnVersion` is the generation id; the producer/reconciliation query
6705:5: * every ACTIVE generation's partitions during a reshard transition window (ÃƒÆ’Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§9.6's runbook

6711:11: * when it can stop double-querying it (the runbook's "atÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â© a janela de materializaÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§ÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â£o
6712:12: * antiga expirar, ~7 dias ÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â  frente no pior caso").

6716:16:  shardCount: number;
6717:17:  /** ISO instant after which this generation no longer needs to be queried (undefined = still active/current). Set when a reshard retires this generation. */

6719:19:}

6721:21:export interface ShardConfig {

6726:26:}
6727:27:
6728:28:export const DEFAULT_SHARD_COUNT = 4;
6729:29:
6730:30:export function defaultShardConfig(): ShardConfig {

6732:32:}
6733:33:
6734:34:/** Generations the producer/reconciliation must query "now" (implementation-blueprint.md

6736:36: * transition window). Excludes legacy generations whose retireAfter has passed. */
6737:37:export function activeGenerations(config: ShardConfig, now: string): ShardGeneration[] {
6738:38:  const stillActiveLegacy = config.legacy.filter((g) => !g.retireAfter || g.retireAfter > now);
6739:39:  return [config.current, ...stillActiveLegacy];
6740:40:}
6741:41:
6742:42:/**

6744:44: * after `retireAfter`, default input by caller - the runbook's ~7 day worst-case
6745:45: * materialization-ahead window), and a new current generation is created with double the
6746:46: * shard count and the next `shardFnVersion`.

6752:52:  };

3:Responds to Codex round 3 (7.4/10, 8 required changes). Everything from rounds 1-3 not
4:contradicted here stands (names, GSI3 port, `SendMessageBatch` handling â€” confirmed "fixed" by
5:Codex round 3, error table shape, claim extraction). This round's unifying fix: **every lease

7:checkpoint, not just checkpoint â€” goes through the SAME outbox+relay mechanism**, closing required

9:
10:## Required change 1+3: unified lease-transition table, ALL transitions outbox-atomic
11:
12:**Every** lease-row write that implies "a message should eventually exist" is now one
13:`TransactWriteItems` containing the lease write AND an `appendToTransaction` outbox Put, using the
14:SAME `SQS_REMINDER_SCAN_CONTINUATION_V1` destination for all of them (a "start" message is simply a
15:continuation with `lastEvaluatedKey: undefined` â€” already true since round 1, now load-bearing:
16:the wire shape doesn't distinguish start from continuation, only the outbox-atomicity guarantee
17:does, uniformly).
18:
19:| Transition | Item write | Condition | Outbox entry? |
20:|---|---|---|---|
21:| **Fresh acquire** (page 1, no prior lease row) | `buildConditionalPut`: `Item: { PK, SK: "LEASE", entityType: "ReminderScanLease", status: "IN_PROGRESS", ownerToken: newToken, leaseUntil: now+200s, lastEvaluatedKey: undefined, pagesProcessed: 0, candidatesPublished: 0, version: 1, purgeAfterTtl: now/1000 + 7*24*3600 }`, `conditionExpression: "attribute_not_exists(PK)"` | row must not exist | YES â€” start message, `lastEvaluatedKey: undefined` |
22:| **Reclaim** (row exists, expired) | Same `buildConditionalPut` shape, `Item.version: 1` reset (a reclaim is a fresh chain, not a continuation of the dead one's counters â€” `pagesProcessed`/`candidatesPublished` reset to 0, new `ownerToken`), `conditionExpression: "status = :inProgress AND leaseUntil < :now"` (values supplied) | row exists, expired | YES â€” start message, `lastEvaluatedKey: undefined` (restart from page 1 â€” the dead chain's `lastEvaluatedKey` is discarded, since `queryGsi3Page` is a pure read and redoing it from the top is simpler and cheap at `limit:200`, and safer than trusting a half-written cursor from a chain that died for an unknown reason) |
23:| **Checkpoint, more pages remain** | `buildUnscopedVersionedUpdate`: `set: { lastEvaluatedKey: nextKey, leaseUntil: now+200s, pagesProcessed: +1, candidatesPublished: +thisPage }`, `expectedVersion` = version this invocation read, `extraConditions: [{ expression: "ownerToken = :myToken AND #cursorCond" }]` where `#cursorCond` is `attribute_not_exists(lastEvaluatedKey)` for a page-1 invocation or `lastEvaluatedKey = :myStartKey` for a continuation invocation â€” **two distinct code branches choosing which condition string to build, never one OR expression** (Codex round 2's exact ask, restated as now-implemented) | ownerToken + cursor match | YES â€” continuation message, `lastEvaluatedKey: nextKey` |
24:| **Checkpoint, last page** (`queryGsi3Page` returned no `LastEvaluatedKey`) | Same builder, `set: { status: "COMPLETED", leaseUntil: now+200s, pagesProcessed: +1, candidatesPublished: +thisPage }`, same ownerToken/cursor condition | ownerToken + cursor match | **NO outbox entry** â€” completion is terminal, nothing should ever be sent next; round 3's example wrongly called `appendToTransaction` unconditionally (Codex's exact catch, fixed: the transaction array only gets the outbox entries pushed inside the `if (nextKey)` branch, never in the `else` branch) |
25:| **Continuation/start message received, but lease already `COMPLETED` or past this cursor** | no write | n/a | ack, no-op, logged `"stale message no-op"` â€” unchanged from round 2/3 |
26:
27:This closes required change 1 completely: a crash between "lease acquired" and "start message sent"
28:is now impossible by the same construction that already closed the page-to-page case â€” the
29:acquire/reclaim Put and the start-message outbox Put commit together or not at all.

31:## Required change 2/10: independent stalled-lease detection â€” extends `reminder-reconciliation`, not a new component
32:
33:Codex correctly proved lookback-only rediscovery has a real hole (a lease whose minute ages out of
34:the 15-minute window before ever being retried). Fix: **lease rows get a GSI6 pointer while
35:`IN_PROGRESS`**, mirroring the EXACT pattern `reminder-reconciliation.ts` already uses for stuck
36:`CLAIMED` occurrences (`GSI6PK_WORKSTATE_CLAIMED` today) â€” `GSI6PK: "SCANLEASE#IN_PROGRESS"`,
37:`GSI6SK: "<leaseUntil-ISO>#<shardFnVersion>#<shardId>#<minuteISO>"` (sortable by expiry, same
38:"query the oldest-expiring first" shape reconciliation's existing claim-expiry pass already relies
39:on), written in every acquire/reclaim/checkpoint transaction above (one more `set`/removed on
40:`COMPLETED`, same transaction, no extra write). **`reminder-reconciliation.ts` gets a genuinely new
41:third pass** (amending, with reasoning, round 1's "no change" expectation â€” the task explicitly
42:allows correcting that expectation, and this is the correction): reusing its EXISTING 5-minute
43:`CLAIMS`-mode schedule (no new EventBridge schedule, no new Lambda), it also queries
44:`GSI6PK = "SCANLEASE#IN_PROGRESS"` for `GSI6SK < now`, and for each hit, runs the SAME reclaim
45:transition as a normal reclaim (new `ownerToken`, fresh start-message outbox entry) â€” this is the
46:row's SECOND possible reclaimer (the next EventBridge tick within lookback is the first,
47:faster path; reconciliation is the backstop that still works after lookback expiry). New metric
48:`ReconciliationScanLeaseReclaimed` (Count, namespace `ExpirationTracker/ReminderReconciliation` â€”
49:existing namespace for that Lambda, confirmed by checking its handler file this round) +
50:CloudWatch alarm at >0/5min (same alarm shape as round 3's, now on the metric that's actually
51:independent â€” reconciliation runs on its own schedule regardless of whether the scan/claim queues
52:have any traffic at all, correctly answering Codex's "must work when queue is empty" requirement).
53:IAM: reconciliation's Lambda already holds `gsi6Read()` (confirmed,
54:`reminder-reconciliation-handler.ts` header comment: "um dos exatamente dois papÃ©is com
55:gsi6Read()") â€” the second role already IS this one, so no new grant, just a new query shape against
56:an index this function already reads.

131:

133:â€” the occurrence update is **always transaction index 0** (a named constant,
134:`OCCURRENCE_UPDATE_TX_INDEX = 0`, exported next to `getCancellationReasonCodes` usage sites so the
135:index is never a magic number at the call site) â€” this holds for BOTH `claimReminderOccurrence`
136:(new extracted function) and `claimChasingOccurrence`. Round 3's test-inventory wording calling
137:`claimChasingOccurrence` "unchanged" is WRONG and retracted: per Codex's citation
138:(`document-chasing-producer.ts:131-135`, today's catch-all `LOST_CLAIM_RACE`), the SAME
139:reason-specific fix applies to it â€” it also switches to
140:`getCancellationReasonCodes(err)[OCCURRENCE_UPDATE_TX_INDEX] === "ConditionalCheckFailed"` as the
141:only true lost-race condition, everything else retried. Both functions change identically; only
142:their surrounding command/event construction (already entity-type-specific today) stays as-is.

144:## Required change 8: rollback â€” two-step, mapping-gated, no acknowledge-and-discard
145:
146:Corrected: rollback is now symmetric with the forward rollout's two-apply shape, not a single env
147:var flip. **Rollback Apply A**: set BOTH the scan queue's and claim queue's event-source-mapping
148:`enabled = false` (Terraform attribute change, each its own resource, no ordering dependency
149:between them since both moving to `false` commutes) â€” this stops BOTH consumers from being invoked
150:at all, so nothing is silently acknowledged-and-discarded (Codex's exact objection: a `LEGACY`-mode
151:no-op handler still `ack`s and deletes the SQS message; disabling the mapping instead means the
152:message is never delivered to any handler, sitting safely in the queue). **Observe**: operator (or
153:a scripted check, not a blocking automated gate for this plan's scope) confirms both queues'
154:`ApproximateNumberOfMessages` + `ApproximateNumberOfMessagesNotVisible` settle near zero OR
155:accepts they won't (a genuine rollback during an active burst may have real backlog) â€” either way,
156:proceed only once mapping-disabled state is confirmed applied (Terraform apply success is
157:sufficient confirmation of THIS step; draining is a monitoring concern, not a blocking gate).
158:**Rollback Apply B**: flip `SCAN_MODE` back to `LEGACY`. Now old code resumes scanning, and neither
159:new consumer can claim concurrently with it (mappings disabled) â€” "exactly one mode live" is true
160:again, both at the code-path level AND the message-consumption level (round 3 only had the former).
161:**Residual queued messages** (scan/claim) are left in place, inert, until either: an operator
162:manually purges the queues (runbook note, not automated), or a future forward-roll re-enables the
163:mappings and they're reprocessed under the SAME idempotency guarantees this whole design provides
164:(stale-cursor no-ops, conditional claim dedup) â€” so leaving them queued is safe, not just
165:inert, if rollback is later reversed.

380:## Required changes 1+2: checkpoint/continuation Ã¢â‚¬â€ outbox-atomic, not send-then-checkpoint
381:
382:**`SQS_REMINDER_SCAN_CONTINUATION_V1` is reinstated in `OutboxDestination`** (round 2 wrongly
383:removed it). Checkpoint transition (after a page's candidates are durably published, see Ã‚Â§7 below)
384:is now ONE `TransactWriteItems`, same shape as `producer.ts:286-306`:
385:```ts
386:const outboxEntries: DynamoTransactPutEntry[] = [];
387:appendToTransaction(outboxEntries, deps.tableName, continuationEvent, "SQS_REMINDER_SCAN_CONTINUATION_V1");
388:await deps.store.transactWrite([
389:  { Update: buildUnscopedVersionedUpdate({ tableName, key: leaseKey, expectedVersion: leaseVersionThisInvocationRead, set: { lastEvaluatedKey: nextKey /* or REMOVE + status: "COMPLETED" on last page */, leaseUntil: now + LEASE_MS, pagesProcessed: pagesProcessed + 1, candidatesPublished: candidatesPublished + thisPageCount }, extraConditions: [{ expression: "ownerToken = :myToken AND #startKeyCond", ... }] }) },
390:  ...outboxEntries,
391:]);
392:```
393:`DispatchOutboxRelay` (DynamoDB Streams, `producer.ts:270`'s existing mechanism) is extended to
394:also recognize `SQS_REMINDER_SCAN_CONTINUATION_V1` and publish to the scan queue instead of the
395:dispatch queue Ã¢â‚¬â€ same relay, same sweeper-recovers-publish-failures guarantee, routed by the
396:existing `destination` discriminator (no new relay Lambda). **Verified this round, not just
397:asserted**: `src/workers/dispatch-outbox-relay/relay.ts:12-14,22-27,122-152` shows the relay is
398:ALREADY a generalized multi-destination router (`senders: Record<OutboxDestination, Sender>`,
399:one sweeper instance covers multiple destinations) Ã¢â‚¬â€ it already recognizes
400:`SQS_REMINDER_DISPATCH_V1` and `SQS_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_V1` side by side, so adding a third
401:`senders` entry for `SQS_REMINDER_SCAN_CONTINUATION_V1` (pointing at the scan queue URL) is the
402:exact, already-precedented extension point Ã¢â‚¬â€ no relay redesign needed. **This closes required change 1's
403:exact failure trace**: a continuation now literally cannot exist in SQS until the checkpoint
404:transaction has committed, so "successor consumed before predecessor checkpoint" is impossible by
405:construction Ã¢â‚¬â€ there is no window where a successor can arrive early, because the successor's own
406:existence is downstream of (caused by) the checkpoint, not concurrent with it. Required change 2's
407:"specify a rigorous successor protocol" is answered by removing the need for one: at-least-once
408:delivery of the SAME continuation (streams relay redelivery, sweeper retry, or SQS standard-queue
409:redelivery) is idempotent because the checkpoint that produced it already advanced
410:`lastEvaluatedKey` Ã¢â‚¬â€ a redelivered continuation's handler re-reads the CURRENT lease row, finds
411:`lastEvaluatedKey` already matches (or is already past) what the message describes as "next to
412:process," and either does the work once (first delivery) or no-ops (subsequent redeliveries,
413:detected by comparing the message's OWN `lastEvaluatedKey` against the row's, exactly as round 2
414:proposed Ã¢â‚¬â€ this piece survives unchanged, now sitting on a sound foundation instead of a broken one).

611:## Required change 13Ã¢â€ â€™ this round's Ã‚Â§: deploy/rollback via explicit env-var toggle
612:
613:Codex's own three suggested options include "a temporary handler-routing/feature switch" Ã¢â‚¬â€ this
614:plan adopts it explicitly, addressing the earlier concern that D-299 "rejected a flag": D-299
615:rejected PERMANENTLY running old and new claim logic concurrently against the same table (a
616:correctness/race concern Ã¢â‚¬â€ doubling the concurrent-claim surface indefinitely). A **deploy-time-only
617:env var** (`SCAN_MODE: "LEGACY" | "PAGED"`, read once at cold start, no per-invocation branching
618:risk) is a materially different, lesser thing: at any given moment exactly ONE mode is live (never
619:both), and the var is deleted entirely (code for `"LEGACY"` removed) in the third, later change Ã¢â‚¬â€
620:it is a rollout mechanism with a defined end, not a standing dual-path architecture.
621:- **Apply 1**: claim queue + consumer (event-source-mapping enabled, inert Ã¢â‚¬â€ nothing publishes to
622:  it), scan queue (event-source-mapping enabled Ã¢â‚¬â€ also inert, nothing publishes to it either, since
623:  `SCAN_MODE=LEGACY` never emits start messages), new port/adapter/handler code deployed but
624:  `SCAN_MODE=LEGACY` at the environment level keeps `reminder-producer-handler.ts` executing
625:  exactly today's `runProducerTick` path. This IS enough to make Apply 1 genuinely inert (Codex's
626:  exact objection to round 2), because the toggle lives in application code reading `process.env`,
627:  not in Terraform resource wiring whose ordering Terraform doesn't guarantee.
628:- **Apply 2**: flips `SCAN_MODE=PAGED` via a Lambda environment variable update Ã¢â‚¬â€ a single
629:  Terraform-managed attribute change, applied atomically to the function configuration (no
630:  cross-resource ordering concern, since it's one resource's one attribute).
631:- **Lease/queue cleanup on rollback**: revert Apply 2's env var back to `LEGACY`. In-flight scan
632:  chains stop producing new checkpoints (no consumer reads them meaningfully once `LEGACY` code
633:  ignores SQS-sourced invocations Ã¢â‚¬â€ the SQS-triggered handler branch checks `SCAN_MODE` too and
634:  no-ops with a log line if rolled back mid-flight, rather than assuming it's never invoked).
635:  Abandoned lease rows expire via `purgeAfterTtl` (corrected attribute name,
636:  `infra/modules/dynamo-table/main.tf:206-208` Ã¢â‚¬â€ round 2's `ttl` typo fixed) at `leaseUntil + 7d`,
637:  unchanged from round 1/2's retention choice. Queued-but-unprocessed scan/claim messages age out
638:  via each queue's normal 4-day retention or get DLQ'd after `maxReceiveCount=5` Ã¢â‚¬â€ both bounded,
639:  self-cleaning, no manual drain step required, though a runbook note (not a blocking step) to
640:  purge the claim queue manually before an unusually long rollback window is worth adding in the
641:  final artifact.

1313:296:12:## Research declaration (research-protocol.md, E-014)
1314:297:13:
1315:298:14:**SIM PARCIAL.** The macro-pattern (decouple scan from claim via two queues) is already
1316:299:15:externally researched and cited in D-299 (AWS Prescriptive Guidance, Lambda+SQS developer guide,
1317:300:16:SQS API reference). What's new at THIS level is a sub-decision AWS has a well-documented but
1318:301:17:non-obvious answer for: **SQS visibility timeout sizing relative to Lambda timeout, and its
1319:302:18:interaction with `maxReceiveCount`/DLQ redelivery for a handler that holds an idempotency lease**.
1320:303:19:This project's own `sqs-worker-queue` module already encodes one specific answer (6x, fixed,
1321:304:20:`maxReceiveCount=5`) as a blanket rule for the dispatch case ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â applying it unmodified to a
1322:305:21:lease-holding consumer needs to be checked against AWS's own guidance on visibility timeout vs.
1323:306:22:in-flight processing time, because a lease-based state machine changes what "redelivery mid-lease"
1324:307:23:means (D-299's own R3ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â€žÂ¢R4 finding). Checklist applied this round, sourced from AWS Lambda Developer
1325:308:24:Guide "Using Lambda with Amazon SQS" (event source mapping / partial batch response) and AWS SQS
1326:309:25:"Amazon SQS visibility timeout" page (both already cited as sources in D-299, re-read here for the
1327:310:26:consumer-timeout-vs-lease-duration angle specifically, no new source needed):
1328:311:27:1. Visibility timeout must exceed **worst-case** processing time, not average ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â for a lease-based
1329:312:28:   consumer, worst case includes lease renewal, not just one page's work.
1330:313:29:2. `maxReceiveCount` ÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â avg processing time bounds how long a poison message cycles before DLQ ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â
1331:314:30:   must be reconciled with lease `leaseUntil` duration so an expired lease and an SQS redelivery
1332:315:31:   don't race in a way that duplicates or drops work (D-299's exact concern, now at the queue-timer
1333:316:32:   level instead of the state-machine level).
1334:317:33:3. Batch size for the scan-continuation queue must stay effectively 1 (see ÃƒÆ’Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§3 below) ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â AWS's own
1335:318:34:   guidance warns partial-batch-failure handling gets materially harder above batch size 1 when
1336:319:35:   messages are causally chained (continuation N+1 must not be visible before N's page commits).
