1403:386:102:"belt AND suspenders" pattern `runProducerTick` already uses for claim races today).
1404:387:103:
1405:388:104:**Renew** (before publishing each continuation) ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â `occ.ts`'s `buildVersionedUpdate` with
1406:389:105:`ConditionExpression: "ownerToken = :myToken AND version = :expectedVersion"`: sets new
1407:390:106:`leaseUntil`, `lastEvaluatedKey`, increments `pagesProcessed`/`candidatesPublished`, bumps
1408:391:107:`version`. **This update happens AFTER the claim-queue `SendMessageBatch` succeeds and BEFORE the
1409:392:108:continuation message is sent** ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â ordering matters: if the process dies between the batch send and
1410:393:109:the lease renew, the next attempt (a fresh SQS redelivery of the SAME scan message, since it never
1411:394:110:completed) re-reads `lastEvaluatedKey` from the STALE lease state (pre-this-page), re-queries the
1412:395:111:same page from `queryGsi3` (deterministic per `lastEvaluatedKey`), and re-publishes the same
1413:396:112:candidates. This is why **claim-queue candidates must be idempotent to redelivery independent of
1414:397:113:this lease** ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â already true by construction, because the claim consumer's own conditional
1415:398:114:`transactWrite` (ÃƒÆ’Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§ below) is the actual idempotency boundary for claiming, not the scan side. The
1416:399:115:lease's job is only to make forward SCAN progress resumable exactly-once-effectively, not to
1417:400:116:dedupe claims (that guarantee already exists one layer down).
1418:401:117:
1419:402:118:**Release** (last page, `queryGsi3` returns no `LastEvaluatedKey`) ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â `buildVersionedUpdate` sets
1420:403:119:`status = "COMPLETED"`, same ownerToken/version condition.
1421:404:120:
1422:405:121:**Expire**: no active "expire" write ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â a lease simply becomes reclaimable once `leaseUntil < now`,
1423:406:122:matched by the Acquire condition above. No separate reconciliation pass is added for this (see ÃƒÆ’Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§6
1424:407:123:ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â `reminder-reconciliation.ts` is untouched; lease reclaim is self-contained inside the scan path,
1425:408:124:triggered by the SAME continuation message that would have fired next, since EventBridge Scheduler
1426:409:125:fires a new tick every minute and a new tick for an ALREADY in-progress shard is the natural
1427:410:126:reclaim trigger ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â see ÃƒÆ’Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§7 for why this is safe rather than racy).
1428:411:127:
1429:412:128:## 3. Timeout/visibility sizing
1430:413:129:
1431:414:130:Fixed module facts (not renegotiable without a `sqs-worker-queue` module change, out of scope
1432:415:131:here): `visibility_timeout_seconds = consumer_timeout_seconds * 6`, `maxReceiveCount = 5` fixed.
1433:416:132:
1434:417:133:- **Scan Lambda timeout**: 30s (one `queryGsi3` page + one `SendMessageBatch` + one lease
1435:418:134:  renew/acquire ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â bounded work, generous margin over p99). ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â€žÂ¢ scan queue visibility timeout = 180s
1436:419:135:  (module-derived, 6x).
1437:420:136:- **Claim Lambda timeout**: 10s (unchanged from today's per-occurrence claim ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â a single `get` +
1438:421:137:  `transactWrite`, same cost as today's inner loop iteration). ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â€žÂ¢ claim queue visibility timeout =
1439:422:138:  60s (module-derived, 6x).
1440:423:139:- **Lease duration** (`leaseUntil - leaseAcquiredAt`): **90s** ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â set independently of the Lambda
1441:424:140:  timeout (it is a business-level mutual-exclusion window, not a retry mechanism) but sized against
1442:425:141:  it with an explicit invariant: **lease duration ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â°Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â¥ 2x scan Lambda timeout** (30sÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â2=60s ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â°Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â¤ 90s),
1443:426:142:  giving one full retry's worth of headroom before a DIFFERENT invocation is allowed to steal the
1444:427:143:  lease, so a slow-but-alive attempt is never pre-empted by its own SQS-triggered retry racing in.
1445:428:144:  Combined with **scan visibility timeout (180s) > lease duration (90s)**, an SQS redelivery of the
1446:429:145:  SAME message can never arrive before the lease it would contend with has already legitimately
1447:430:146:  expired ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â removing the specific race D-299 R3 found (two live workers believing they both hold
1448:431:147:  the lease) by construction, not by luck.
1449:432:148:- **`maxReceiveCount=5` (fixed)** on the scan queue means a poison continuation message cycles for
1450:433:149:  up to 5ÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â180s = 900s (15 min) before DLQ ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â acceptable, since EventBridge Scheduler fires a new
1451:434:150:  tick every 60s regardless, so a stuck shard's lease will be reclaimed by a FRESH tick's message
1452:435:151:  well before the poison copy DLQs; the DLQ path exists for the case where `queryGsi3` itself is
1453:436:152:  erroring (data/query bug), not for ordinary transient contention.
1454:437:153:- **Batch size**: scan queue consumer batch size = **1** (continuation messages are causally
1455:438:154:  chained per shard ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â processing two "next page" messages for the same shard concurrently is
1456:439:155:  exactly the race this design eliminates via the lease, so the event-source-mapping must not
1457:440:156:  create that race by delivering >1 at once). Claim queue consumer batch size = **10** (candidates
1458:441:157:  are independent per occurrence, matches `reminder-dispatch`'s existing batch size ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â confirmed
1459:442:158:  against `infra/main.tf`'s `reminder_dispatch_from_queue` event source mapping).
1460:443:159:- **Concurrency invariant** (D-299, now with numbers): scan queue
1461:444:160:  `reserved_concurrent_executions` = number of shards (`defaultShardConfig()`'s shard count,
1462:445:161:  confirmed = `DEFAULT_SHARD_COUNT = 4` in `src/modules/reminder/domain/shard-config.ts`) ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â one in-flight scan per shard by
1463:446:162:  construction (the lease already enforces this logically; the Lambda concurrency cap is defense in
1464:447:163:  depth, cheap to set). Claim queue `reserved_concurrent_executions` = **16** (ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â°Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â¥ sum of scan's
1465:448:164:  per-page candidate fan-out ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â a page of `queryGsi3` batches up to 25 candidates per
1466:449:165:  `SendMessageBatch` call, ÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â4 shards worst-case-concurrent = 100 theoretical peak sends, but claim
1467:450:166:  Lambda p50 is <200ms so 16 concurrent claim workers clears a 100-item burst in ~1.3s ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â matches
1468:451:167:  PERF-12's own 10k-in-a-minute volume target with margin, verified against PERF-12's report
1469:452:168:  numbers in `docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-structural-fix-scoping/` round artifacts).

1567:550:266:## 7. Migration/rollout
1568:551:267:
1569:552:268:Big-bang cutover, not staged, for a concrete reason: the scan and claim halves are not
1570:553:269:independently useful (a scan queue with no claim consumer just accumulates candidates; a claim
1571:554:270:consumer with no new-shape scan producer never receives anything) ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â there's no safe intermediate
1572:555:271:state to stage through, unlike, say, a dual-write migration. Sequencing:
1573:556:272:1. Deploy claim consumer Lambda + claim queue (inert ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â nothing publishes to it yet).
1574:557:273:2. Deploy scan queue (inert ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â nothing subscribes to the OLD producer's shard-loop yet, since it
1575:558:274:   doesn't publish to it).
1576:559:275:3. Deploy the MODIFIED `reminder-producer-handler.ts` (now page-based) in the SAME release as step
1577:560:276:   1/2's infra ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â this is the actual cutover moment; the old monolithic-per-shard loop code path is
1578:561:277:   deleted in this same change, not kept behind a flag (D-299 didn't ask for a flag, and a flag
1579:562:278:   here would mean maintaining two claim code paths against the same table, doubling the
1580:563:279:   concurrent-claim race surface this whole fix targets).
1581:564:280:4. **Occurrences already `SCHEDULED` at cutover**: confirmed safe, with reasoning ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â `SCHEDULED`
1582:565:281:   occurrences are discovered by `queryGsi3`, not by any in-flight queue state; the OLD mechanism's
1583:566:282:   only in-flight artifact at cutover is whatever's already sitting in the OLD single-invocation
1584:567:283:   claim loop of a tick that started before deploy (which either finishes normally before the
1585:568:284:   deploy completes, since Lambda in-flight invocations aren't killed by a code update, or times
1586:569:285:   out and is picked up fresh by the NEW scan mechanism's next tick ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â no occurrence-level state is

3398:2381:1792:# --- UploadFinalizerWorker: S3 event (via queue) -> validate + invoke ParserSandbox ---------
3399:2382:1793:
3400:2383:1794:# Real bug found via Camada 3 (2026-08-22): UploadFinalizerWorker only had READ access to the
3401:2384:1795:# quarantine bucket, but advanceAfterEvidence() (called identically by both workers) performs
3402:2385:1796:# the actual quarantine->clean promotion copy whichever worker's evidence completes the pair
3403:2386:1797:# LAST - which is not always MalwareResultWorker. A real upload where the finalizer's own
3404:2387:1798:# evidence-persist step landed after the malware scan result hit exactly this: the finalizer
3405:2388:1799:# won the PROMOTE race and got a real AccessDenied trying s3:PutObject on the clean bucket.
3406:2389:1800:# Both workers need IDENTICAL object-access permissions for this reason - kept as two
3407:2390:1801:# separately-named data sources (not a single shared one) so each function's IAM role
3408:2391:1802:# document stays self-explanatory in `aws iam` output, but the statements are deliberately
3409:2392:1803:# identical to malware_result_object_access below.
3410:2393:1804:data "aws_iam_policy_document" "upload_finalizer_object_access" {
3411:2394:1805:  statement {
3412:2395:1806:    sid       = "ReadDeleteQuarantineObjects"
3413:2396:1807:    effect    = "Allow"
3414:2397:1808:    actions   = ["s3:GetObject", "s3:GetObjectVersion", "s3:DeleteObjectVersion"]
3415:2398:1809:    resources = ["${module.document_buckets.quarantine_bucket_arn}/*"]
3416:2399:1810:  }
3417:2400:1811:  statement {
3418:2401:1812:    # Real bug found via Camada 3 (2026-08-22): advanceAfterEvidence() calls headObject() on
3419:2402:1813:    # the clean bucket right after copyObject() to VERIFY the promotion copy actually landed
3420:2403:1814:    # before confirming CLEAN - S3's HeadObject API requires the s3:GetObject IAM action (a

6418:5401:FILE src/shared/observability/context.ts
6419:5402:1:/**
6420:5403:2: * Request-scoped correlation context via AsyncLocalStorage (m5-observability-design.md #2).
6421:5404:3: * runWithContext is called once per record for batch handlers (SQS, DynamoDB Streams, sweeper) -
6422:5405:4: * never once per invocation for those - so context never leaks across records in the same batch.
6423:5406:5: */
6424:5407:6:import { AsyncLocalStorage } from "node:async_hooks";
6425:5408:7:
6426:5409:8:export interface RequestContext {
6427:5410:9:  correlationId: string;
6428:5411:10:  tenantId?: string;
6429:5412:11:  requestId?: string;
6430:5413:12:}
6431:5414:13:
6432:5415:14:const storage = new AsyncLocalStorage<RequestContext>();
6433:5416:15:
6434:5417:16:export function runWithContext<T>(context: RequestContext, fn: () => T): T {
6435:5418:17:  return storage.run(context, fn);
6436:5419:18:}
6437:5420:19:
6438:5421:20:export function getContext(): RequestContext | undefined {
6439:5422:21:  return storage.getStore();
6440:5423:22:}
6441:5424:23:
6442:5425:24:/**
6443:5426:25: * m5-observability-design.md #2: correlationId for an SQS record whose sender (relay/
6444:5427:26: * sweeper's composition-root senders, src/runtime/aws/composition/*.ts) propagates the
6445:5428:27: * original business correlationId via this exact MessageAttribute name - see
6446:5429:28: * outboxRecordCorrelationId (src/shared/outbox/outbox.ts) for the sender side of this same
6447:5430:29: * contract. Falls back to the SQS messageId only for a message that never got the
6448:5431:30: * attribute (pre-M5 in-flight, or a queue whose producer has no upstream correlationId to

6589:5572:63:interface ScopedVersionedUpdateInput {
6590:5573:64:  tableName: string;
6591:5574:65:  key: EntityKey;
6592:5575:66:  expectedVersion: number;
6593:5576:67:  set: Record<string, unknown>;
6594:5577:68:  remove?: string[];
6595:5578:69:  now?: string;
6596:5579:70:  extraConditions?: Array<{ expression: string; names?: Record<string, string>; values?: Record<string, unknown> }>;
6597:5580:71:}
6598:5581:72:
6599:5582:73:/**
6600:5583:74: * Private core shared by `buildVersionedUpdate()` (tenant-fenced, every ordinary business
6601:5584:75: * entity) and `buildAccountScopedVersionedUpdate()` (D-197 fatia 3/5: WhatsApp `WebhookInbox`,
6602:5585:76: * the first entity in this repo with no tenant at all - see
6603:5586:77: * `docs/architecture/reviews/whatsapp-channel-scoping/webhook-inbox-purge-scoping/` for the
6604:5587:78: * 3-round Claude<->Codex protocol, both final notes >=9.0, that decided this shape). The ONLY
6605:5588:79: * difference between the two public builders is which attribute anchors the scope fence
6606:5589:80: * (`tenantId` vs `accountId`) - version increment, `updatedAt`, SET/REMOVE generation,
6607:5590:81: * `extraConditions` composition and placeholder-collision detection are a single implementation,
6608:5591:82: * never duplicated, so the two builders can never drift apart on anything but their fence.
6609:5592:83: */
6610:5593:84:function buildScopedVersionedUpdate(input: ScopedVersionedUpdateInput, scope: ScopeCondition): DynamoUpdateCommandInput {
6611:5594:85:  const now = input.now ?? new Date().toISOString();
6612:5595:86:
6613:5596:87:  const names: Record<string, string> = {
6614:5597:88:    "#version": "version",
6615:5598:89:    [scope.namePlaceholder]: scope.attributeName,
6616:5599:90:    "#updatedAt": "updatedAt",
6617:5600:91:  };
6618:5601:92:  const values: Record<string, unknown> = {
6619:5602:93:    ":expectedVersion": input.expectedVersion,
6620:5603:94:    [scope.valuePlaceholder]: scope.value,
6621:5604:95:    ":one": 1,
6622:5605:96:    ":now": now,
6623:5606:97:  };
6624:5607:98:
6625:5608:99:  const setClauses = ["#version = #version + :one", "#updatedAt = :now"];
6626:5609:100:  let i = 0;
6627:5610:101:  for (const [field, value] of Object.entries(input.set)) {
6628:5611:102:    const nameKey = `#set${i}`;
6629:5612:103:    const valueKey = `:set${i}`;
6630:5613:104:    names[nameKey] = field;
6631:5614:105:    values[valueKey] = value;
6632:5615:106:    setClauses.push(`${nameKey} = ${valueKey}`);
6633:5616:107:    i += 1;
6634:5617:108:  }
6635:5618:109:
6636:5619:110:  const removeClauses: string[] = [];
6637:5620:111:  let j = 0;
6638:5621:112:  for (const field of input.remove ?? []) {
6639:5622:113:    const nameKey = `#rem${j}`;
6640:5623:114:    names[nameKey] = field;
6641:5624:115:    removeClauses.push(nameKey);
6642:5625:116:    j += 1;
6643:5626:117:  }
6644:5627:118:
6645:5628:119:  const expression =
6646:5629:120:    removeClauses.length > 0
6647:5630:121:      ? `SET ${setClauses.join(", ")} REMOVE ${removeClauses.join(", ")}`
6648:5631:122:      : `SET ${setClauses.join(", ")}`;
6649:5632:123:
6650:5633:124:  const baseConditionParts = ["attribute_exists(PK)", "attribute_exists(SK)", "#version = :expectedVersion", `${scope.namePlaceholder} = ${scope.valuePlaceholder}`];
6651:5634:125:  for (const extra of input.extraConditions ?? []) {
6652:5635:126:    for (const [nameKey, name] of Object.entries(extra.names ?? {})) {
6653:5636:127:      if (nameKey in names) throw new Error(`extraConditions name placeholder collides with a reserved/generated key: ${nameKey}`);
6654:5637:128:      names[nameKey] = name;
6655:5638:129:    }
6656:5639:130:    for (const [valueKey, value] of Object.entries(extra.values ?? {})) {
6657:5640:131:      if (valueKey in values) throw new Error(`extraConditions value placeholder collides with a reserved/generated key: ${valueKey}`);
6658:5641:132:      values[valueKey] = value;
6659:5642:133:    }
6660:5643:134:    baseConditionParts.push(`(${extra.expression})`);
6661:5644:135:  }
6662:5645:136:
6663:5646:137:  return {
6664:5647:138:    TableName: input.tableName,
6665:5648:139:    Key: input.key,
6666:5649:140:    UpdateExpression: expression,
6667:5650:141:    ConditionExpression: baseConditionParts.join(" AND "),
6668:5651:142:    ExpressionAttributeNames: names,
6669:5652:143:    ExpressionAttributeValues: values,
6670:5653:144:  };
6671:5654:145:}
6672:5655:146:
6673:5656:147:/**
6674:5657:148: * Builds an UpdateItem input enforcing implementation-blueprint.md #5.2's exact
6675:5658:149: * ConditionExpression: attribute_exists(PK) AND attribute_exists(SK) AND
6676:5659:150: * #version = :expectedVersion AND #tenantId = :tenantId, and increments version atomically.
6677:5660:151: * Contractually unchanged by the account-scoped sibling below - same signature, same generated
6678:5661:152: * expression, byte-for-byte, for every one of this repo's ~40 existing call sites.
6679:5662:153: */
6680:5663:154:export function buildVersionedUpdate(input: VersionedUpdateInput): DynamoUpdateCommandInput {

6801:5784:275:export function buildVersionedDelete(input: {

7327:6310:119:function minuteFloor(d: Date): Date {
7328:6311:120:  return new Date(Math.floor(d.getTime() / 60_000) * 60_000);
7329:6312:121:}
7330:6313:122:
7331:6314:123:/**
7332:6315:124: * PERF-12 1k load test finding (docs/engineering/performance/results/PERF-12-async-pipeline-1k.md):
7333:6316:125: * this loop used to process one occurrence at a time - one `store.get` + one
7334:6317:126: * `store.transactWrite` per occurrence, fully sequential - inside a Lambda with (at the time)
7335:6318:127: * a 10s timeout. With ~250 occurrences concentrated in one shard/minute under a realistic
7336:6319:128: * burst, that budget was nowhere near enough, the function was killed mid-loop repeatedly, and
7337:6320:129: * occurrences that hadn't been claimed yet eventually aged out of the lookback window,
7338:6321:130: * permanently stuck in SCHEDULED. Bounded concurrency here mirrors the exact pattern already
7339:6322:131: * used for the same reason in reminder-dispatch-handler.ts (D-170) - each occurrence's own
7340:6323:132: * `transactWrite` stays a single, independent atomic conditional claim (never merged across
7341:6324:133: * occurrences), so parallelizing here does not touch the transactional or idempotency
7342:6325:134: * guarantees of any individual claim, only how many claims run concurrently. A plain numeric
7343:6326:135: * constant, not unbounded `Promise.all`, to keep the burst of concurrent DynamoDB round trips
7344:6327:136: * per invocation predictable.
7345:6328:137: */
7346:6329:138:const PRODUCER_CLAIM_CONCURRENCY = 8;

7353:6336:145: * independent reasons, checked in this order for a stable, deterministic message:

7361:6344:153:  if (result.failed.length > 0) {
7362:6345:154:    return { alarm: true, reason: `reminder-producer: ${result.failed.length} occurrence(s) failed to claim` };
7363:6346:155:  }

7367:6350:159:/** Runs one producer tick for wall-clock minute `tickMinute` (already floored to the minute by the caller/Lambda trigger). */
7368:6351:160:export async function runProducerTick(deps: ProducerDeps, tickMinute: Date): Promise<ProducerTickResult> {
7369:6352:161:  const generations = activeGenerations(deps.shardConfig, deps.now());
7370:6353:162:  const lookback = deps.lookbackMinutes ?? 15;
7371:6354:163:  const claimTtlMs = deps.claimTtlMs ?? 2 * 60_000;
7372:6355:164:
7373:6356:165:  const minutesToScan: Date[] = [];
7374:6357:166:  for (let i = lookback; i >= 0; i--) {
7375:6358:167:    minutesToScan.push(minuteFloor(new Date(tickMinute.getTime() - i * 60_000)));
7376:6359:168:  }
7377:6360:169:

7381:6364:173:  let unknownEntityType = 0;
7382:6365:174:  let scanned = 0;
7383:6366:175:  let partitions = 0;
7384:6367:176:
7385:6368:177:  // Dedup guard: the same occurrence could show up in more than one scanned minute only if
7386:6369:178:  // materialization ever wrote it under a stale bucket, which shouldn't happen - but a
7387:6370:179:  // Set guards against double-claiming within a single tick regardless.
7388:6371:180:  const seen = new Set<string>();
7389:6372:181:
7390:6373:182:  for (const minute of minutesToScan) {
7391:6374:183:    for (const generation of generations) {
7392:6375:184:      const partitionKeys = gsi3PartitionsForMinute(minute, generation.shardCount);
7393:6376:185:      partitions += partitionKeys.length;
7394:6377:186:      for (const gsi3pk of partitionKeys) {
7395:6378:187:        const rows = await deps.store.queryGsi3<{ PK: string; SK: string; GSI3SK: string }>({ gsi3pk });
7396:6379:188:        // PERF-12: this used to be `for (const row of rows)`, one `get`+`transactWrite` pair
7397:6380:189:        // processed strictly sequentially - see PRODUCER_CLAIM_CONCURRENCY's doc comment for
7398:6381:190:        // why bounded concurrency replaces that here. `seen`/`claimed`/`failed`/
7399:6382:191:        // `chasingClaimed`/counters are shared mutable state across concurrent callbacks, but
7400:6383:192:        // every access happens either synchronously (no `await` in between, so the JS event
7401:6384:193:        // loop cannot interleave two callbacks' synchronous sections) or as an atomic
7402:6385:194:        // push/increment - never a race in practice under Node's single-threaded model.
7403:6386:195:        await mapWithConcurrency(rows, PRODUCER_CLAIM_CONCURRENCY, async (row) => {
7404:6387:196:          scanned += 1;
7405:6388:197:
7406:6389:198:          // M10 cluster 4: try the chasing shape FIRST (never throws, `undefined` on no
7407:6390:199:          // match) - the reminder branch below is completely unchanged otherwise.
7408:6391:200:          const chasingParsed = parseChasingGsi3Sk(row.GSI3SK);
7409:6392:201:          if (chasingParsed) {

7411:6394:203:            seen.add(chasingParsed.occurrenceId);

7413:6396:205:              const outcome = await claimChasingOccurrence(
7414:6397:206:                { store: deps.store, tableName: deps.tableName, now: deps.now, claimTtlMs, newEventId: deps.newEventId, correlationId: deps.correlationId },
7415:6398:207:                { PK: row.PK, SK: row.SK },
7416:6399:208:              );
7417:6400:209:              if (outcome.kind === "CLAIMED") chasingClaimed.push(outcome.command);
7418:6401:210:              // SKIPPED_NOT_SCHEDULED / LOST_CLAIM_RACE: not failures, same as the reminder path below.
7419:6402:211:            } catch (err) {
7420:6403:212:              failed.push({ occurrenceId: chasingParsed.occurrenceId, tenantId: chasingParsed.tenantId, error: err });
7421:6404:213:            }

7424:6407:216:

7426:6409:218:          try {

7428:6411:220:          } catch {

9417:8400:12:## Research declaration (research-protocol.md, E-014)
9418:8401:13:
9419:8402:14:**SIM PARCIAL.** The macro-pattern (decouple scan from claim via two queues) is already
9420:8403:15:externally researched and cited in D-299 (AWS Prescriptive Guidance, Lambda+SQS developer guide,
9421:8404:16:SQS API reference). What's new at THIS level is a sub-decision AWS has a well-documented but
9422:8405:17:non-obvious answer for: **SQS visibility timeout sizing relative to Lambda timeout, and its
9423:8406:18:interaction with `maxReceiveCount`/DLQ redelivery for a handler that holds an idempotency lease**.
9424:8407:19:This project's own `sqs-worker-queue` module already encodes one specific answer (6x, fixed,
9425:8408:20:`maxReceiveCount=5`) as a blanket rule for the dispatch case ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â applying it unmodified to a
9426:8409:21:lease-holding consumer needs to be checked against AWS's own guidance on visibility timeout vs.
9427:8410:22:in-flight processing time, because a lease-based state machine changes what "redelivery mid-lease"
9428:8411:23:means (D-299's own R3ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â€žÂ¢R4 finding). Checklist applied this round, sourced from AWS Lambda Developer
9429:8412:24:Guide "Using Lambda with Amazon SQS" (event source mapping / partial batch response) and AWS SQS
9430:8413:25:"Amazon SQS visibility timeout" page (both already cited as sources in D-299, re-read here for the
9431:8414:26:consumer-timeout-vs-lease-duration angle specifically, no new source needed):
9432:8415:27:1. Visibility timeout must exceed **worst-case** processing time, not average ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â for a lease-based
9433:8416:28:   consumer, worst case includes lease renewal, not just one page's work.
9434:8417:29:2. `maxReceiveCount` ÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â avg processing time bounds how long a poison message cycles before DLQ ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â
9435:8418:30:   must be reconciled with lease `leaseUntil` duration so an expired lease and an SQS redelivery
9436:8419:31:   don't race in a way that duplicates or drops work (D-299's exact concern, now at the queue-timer
9437:8420:32:   level instead of the state-machine level).
9438:8421:33:3. Batch size for the scan-continuation queue must stay effectively 1 (see ÃƒÆ’Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§3 below) ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â AWS's own
9439:8422:34:   guidance warns partial-batch-failure handling gets materially harder above batch size 1 when
9440:8423:35:   messages are causally chained (continuation N+1 must not be visible before N's page commits).
9441:8424:36:
9442:8425:37:## 1. Names
9443:8426:38:
9444:8427:39:Following `infra/main.tf`'s existing convention (`module "reminder_producer"` /
9445:8428:40:`function_name = "${local.name_prefix}-reminder-producer"`, and `reminder-dispatch`'s two-worker
9446:8429:41:pattern: `module.dispatch_queue` + `module.reminder_dispatch`):

9476:8459:71:## 2. Page-lease state machine
9477:8460:72:
9478:8461:73:**Item** (main table, single-table design ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â PK/SK pattern matches existing shard-scan items in
9479:8462:74:`dynamodb-reminder-producer-store.ts`, confirmed against that file):
9480:8463:75:
9481:8464:76:```
9482:8465:77:PK: SCAN#<shardId>#<tickMinuteISO>     e.g. SCAN#3#2026-09-14T22:31:00Z
9483:8466:78:SK: LEASE
9484:8467:79:entityType: "ReminderScanLease"
9485:8468:80:status: "IN_PROGRESS" | "COMPLETED"
9486:8469:81:ownerToken: string (randomUUID, one per Lambda invocation attempt ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â NOT per SQS messageId,
9487:8470:82:            so a redelivered SQS message that re-enters the same invocation semantics gets a
9488:8471:83:            fresh token and must re-win the conditional acquire, closing the exact silent-drop
9489:8472:84:            hole D-299 R3 found in the stateless-fence design)
9490:8473:85:leaseUntil: number (epoch ms)
9491:8474:86:lastEvaluatedKey: string | undefined (JSON-serialized DynamoDB ExclusiveStartKey for queryGsi3,
9492:8475:87:            undefined on the first page, present on every continuation)
9493:8476:88:pagesProcessed: number
9494:8477:89:candidatesPublished: number
9495:8478:90:version: number (occ.ts optimistic concurrency, same convention as every other mutable item)
9496:8479:91:ttl: epoch seconds, 7 days after leaseUntil ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â cheap cleanup, matches this project's existing TTL
9497:8480:92:     convention on other transient coordination items (checked against `defaultShardConfig()`'s
9498:8481:93:     neighbors in dynamodb-reminder-producer-store.ts)
9499:8482:94:```
9500:8483:95:
9501:8484:96:**Acquire** (first page of a shard/minute, or reclaim after expiry) ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â `occ.ts`'s
9502:8485:97:`buildConditionalPut` with:
9503:8486:98:`ConditionExpression: "attribute_not_exists(PK) OR (status = :inProgress AND leaseUntil < :now) OR status = :completedNoop"`
9504:8487:99:ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â the third arm exists only to make a duplicate "start" message (a Scheduler retry firing the same
9505:8488:100:shard/minute twice) a safe no-op rather than an error; it still writes nothing new when already
9506:8489:101:`COMPLETED` (checked in application code before the Put, not relied on as a silent race ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â same
9507:8490:102:"belt AND suspenders" pattern `runProducerTick` already uses for claim races today).
9508:8491:103:
9509:8492:104:**Renew** (before publishing each continuation) ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â `occ.ts`'s `buildVersionedUpdate` with
9510:8493:105:`ConditionExpression: "ownerToken = :myToken AND version = :expectedVersion"`: sets new
9511:8494:106:`leaseUntil`, `lastEvaluatedKey`, increments `pagesProcessed`/`candidatesPublished`, bumps
9512:8495:107:`version`. **This update happens AFTER the claim-queue `SendMessageBatch` succeeds and BEFORE the
9513:8496:108:continuation message is sent** ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â ordering matters: if the process dies between the batch send and
9514:8497:109:the lease renew, the next attempt (a fresh SQS redelivery of the SAME scan message, since it never
9515:8498:110:completed) re-reads `lastEvaluatedKey` from the STALE lease state (pre-this-page), re-queries the
9516:8499:111:same page from `queryGsi3` (deterministic per `lastEvaluatedKey`), and re-publishes the same
9517:8500:112:candidates. This is why **claim-queue candidates must be idempotent to redelivery independent of
9518:8501:113:this lease** ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â already true by construction, because the claim consumer's own conditional
9519:8502:114:`transactWrite` (ÃƒÆ’Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§ below) is the actual idempotency boundary for claiming, not the scan side. The
9520:8503:115:lease's job is only to make forward SCAN progress resumable exactly-once-effectively, not to
9521:8504:116:dedupe claims (that guarantee already exists one layer down).
9522:8505:117:
9523:8506:118:**Release** (last page, `queryGsi3` returns no `LastEvaluatedKey`) ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â `buildVersionedUpdate` sets
9524:8507:119:`status = "COMPLETED"`, same ownerToken/version condition.
9525:8508:120:
9526:8509:121:**Expire**: no active "expire" write ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â a lease simply becomes reclaimable once `leaseUntil < now`,
9527:8510:122:matched by the Acquire condition above. No separate reconciliation pass is added for this (see ÃƒÆ’Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§6
9528:8511:123:ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â `reminder-reconciliation.ts` is untouched; lease reclaim is self-contained inside the scan path,
9529:8512:124:triggered by the SAME continuation message that would have fired next, since EventBridge Scheduler
9530:8513:125:fires a new tick every minute and a new tick for an ALREADY in-progress shard is the natural
9531:8514:126:reclaim trigger ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â see ÃƒÆ’Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§7 for why this is safe rather than racy).
9532:8515:127:
9533:8516:128:## 3. Timeout/visibility sizing
9534:8517:129:
9535:8518:130:Fixed module facts (not renegotiable without a `sqs-worker-queue` module change, out of scope
9536:8519:131:here): `visibility_timeout_seconds = consumer_timeout_seconds * 6`, `maxReceiveCount = 5` fixed.
9537:8520:132:
9538:8521:133:- **Scan Lambda timeout**: 30s (one `queryGsi3` page + one `SendMessageBatch` + one lease
9539:8522:134:  renew/acquire ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â bounded work, generous margin over p99). ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â€žÂ¢ scan queue visibility timeout = 180s
9540:8523:135:  (module-derived, 6x).
9541:8524:136:- **Claim Lambda timeout**: 10s (unchanged from today's per-occurrence claim ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â a single `get` +
9542:8525:137:  `transactWrite`, same cost as today's inner loop iteration). ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â€žÂ¢ claim queue visibility timeout =
9543:8526:138:  60s (module-derived, 6x).
9544:8527:139:- **Lease duration** (`leaseUntil - leaseAcquiredAt`): **90s** ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â set independently of the Lambda
9545:8528:140:  timeout (it is a business-level mutual-exclusion window, not a retry mechanism) but sized against
9546:8529:141:  it with an explicit invariant: **lease duration ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â°Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â¥ 2x scan Lambda timeout** (30sÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â2=60s ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â°Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â¤ 90s),
9547:8530:142:  giving one full retry's worth of headroom before a DIFFERENT invocation is allowed to steal the
9548:8531:143:  lease, so a slow-but-alive attempt is never pre-empted by its own SQS-triggered retry racing in.
9549:8532:144:  Combined with **scan visibility timeout (180s) > lease duration (90s)**, an SQS redelivery of the
9550:8533:145:  SAME message can never arrive before the lease it would contend with has already legitimately
9551:8534:146:  expired ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â removing the specific race D-299 R3 found (two live workers believing they both hold
9552:8535:147:  the lease) by construction, not by luck.
9553:8536:148:- **`maxReceiveCount=5` (fixed)** on the scan queue means a poison continuation message cycles for
9554:8537:149:  up to 5ÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â180s = 900s (15 min) before DLQ ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â acceptable, since EventBridge Scheduler fires a new
9555:8538:150:  tick every 60s regardless, so a stuck shard's lease will be reclaimed by a FRESH tick's message
9556:8539:151:  well before the poison copy DLQs; the DLQ path exists for the case where `queryGsi3` itself is
9557:8540:152:  erroring (data/query bug), not for ordinary transient contention.
9558:8541:153:- **Batch size**: scan queue consumer batch size = **1** (continuation messages are causally
9559:8542:154:  chained per shard ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â processing two "next page" messages for the same shard concurrently is
9560:8543:155:  exactly the race this design eliminates via the lease, so the event-source-mapping must not
9561:8544:156:  create that race by delivering >1 at once). Claim queue consumer batch size = **10** (candidates
9562:8545:157:  are independent per occurrence, matches `reminder-dispatch`'s existing batch size ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â confirmed
9563:8546:158:  against `infra/main.tf`'s `reminder_dispatch_from_queue` event source mapping).
9564:8547:159:- **Concurrency invariant** (D-299, now with numbers): scan queue
9565:8548:160:  `reserved_concurrent_executions` = number of shards (`defaultShardConfig()`'s shard count,
9566:8549:161:  confirmed = `DEFAULT_SHARD_COUNT = 4` in `src/modules/reminder/domain/shard-config.ts`) ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â one in-flight scan per shard by
9567:8550:162:  construction (the lease already enforces this logically; the Lambda concurrency cap is defense in
9568:8551:163:  depth, cheap to set). Claim queue `reserved_concurrent_executions` = **16** (ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â°Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â¥ sum of scan's
9569:8552:164:  per-page candidate fan-out ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â a page of `queryGsi3` batches up to 25 candidates per
9570:8553:165:  `SendMessageBatch` call, ÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â4 shards worst-case-concurrent = 100 theoretical peak sends, but claim
9571:8554:166:  Lambda p50 is <200ms so 16 concurrent claim workers clears a 100-item burst in ~1.3s ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â matches
9572:8555:167:  PERF-12's own 10k-in-a-minute volume target with margin, verified against PERF-12's report
9573:8556:168:  numbers in `docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-structural-fix-scoping/` round artifacts).

9575:8558:170:## 4. Tracing/logging/metrics/errors/outbox/writes ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â concrete
9576:8559:171:
9577:8560:172:- **Correlation ID propagation**: the ORIGINAL scan tick's `randomUUID()` (today's

9591:8574:186:  `"reminder-scan page complete"` (fields: `shardId`, `tickMinute`, `pageNumber`,

9609:8592:204:    duplicating).
9610:8593:205:- **Error taxonomy** (`app-error.ts`): a lease acquire race that loses is NOT an error (expected
9611:8594:206:  contention, logged/metric'd only). A `queryGsi3` failure inside the scan page throws the SAME
9612:8595:207:  taxonomy the current handler already uses (`ValidationError` for bad continuation payload shape,
9613:8596:208:  unchanged AppError subclasses for downstream failures ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â no new subclass needed, confirmed by
9614:8597:209:  reading the union in `app-error.ts`; if a future round finds a gap, add
9615:8598:210:  `ReminderLeaseConflictError extends AppError` only if contention needs to surface as a retryable
9616:8599:211:  error rather than a logged no-op ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â deferred as a round-2 open question, not assumed here).
9617:8600:212:- **Outbox**: candidates and the continuation message are **NOT** written via the transactional
9618:8601:213:  outbox pattern, and this is a deliberate deviation from AGENTS.md's "critical side-effect in the
9619:8602:214:  same transaction as the aggregate write" rule ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â because there IS no aggregate write at scan time
9620:8603:215:  (the scan step only reads GSI3 and writes its OWN lease item; the occurrence aggregate write only
9621:8604:216:  happens later, in the claim consumer). The outbox pattern's applicability is at the CLAIM step:
9622:8605:217:  the claim consumer's existing `get`+`transactWrite` (unchanged from today) is the aggregate
9623:8606:218:  write, and it already should (today's code should be checked, not assumed ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â round 2 action item)
9624:8607:219:  carry its resulting event via the SAME `TransactWriteItems`, exactly like `SQS_REMINDER_DISPATCH_V1`
9625:8608:220:  today. Round 1 conclusion: **outbox governs the claimÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â€žÂ¢dispatch boundary (unchanged from today),
9626:8609:221:  not the scanÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â€žÂ¢claim boundary (new, and necessarily a direct `SendMessageBatch`, not outbox-mediated,
9627:8610:222:  because outbox requires a DynamoDB transaction and the scan step's transaction is the lease
9628:8611:223:  write, which is unrelated to the individual candidates being published)**.

infra\modules\reminder-schedule\main.tf-1-# EventBridge Scheduler wiring — Terraform equivalent of infra/lib/reminder-schedule.ts.
infra\modules\reminder-schedule\main.tf-2-#
infra\modules\reminder-schedule\main.tf-3-# CRITICAL CONTRACT (bug found by a previous Codex implementation review of the CDK code,
infra\modules\reminder-schedule\main.tf-4-# not reintroduced here): EventBridge Scheduler's Lambda target does NOT wrap the payload in
infra\modules\reminder-schedule\main.tf-5-# a `detail` envelope the way legacy EventBridge Rules do — whatever `input` is set to
infra\modules\reminder-schedule\main.tf-6-# becomes the event object handed to the Lambda directly. Every schedule below sets an
infra\modules\reminder-schedule\main.tf-7-# explicit top-level `input` matching exactly what its handler reads (`event.mode`,
infra\modules\reminder-schedule\main.tf:8:# `event.scheduledTime` — see reminder-producer-handler.ts / reminder-reconciliation-
infra\modules\reminder-schedule\main.tf-9-# handler.ts), never `event.detail.*` / `event.time` (those are Rule-shaped fields that
infra\modules\reminder-schedule\main.tf-10-# don't exist here). `<aws.scheduler.scheduled-time>` is a Scheduler context attribute,
infra\modules\reminder-schedule\main.tf-11-# substituted at invoke time with the schedule's fire time (ISO-8601 UTC).
infra\modules\reminder-schedule\main.tf-12-#
infra\modules\reminder-schedule\main.tf-13-# REAL BUG found and fixed 2026-08-21 via Camada 3 evidence (live CloudWatch logs, not a
infra\modules\reminder-schedule\main.tf-14-# test): `jsonencode()` HTML-escapes the angle-bracket characters to their \uXXXX form (Go's
infra\modules\reminder-schedule\main.tf-15-# encoding/json default, which Terraform's jsonencode inherits) - EventBridge Scheduler's
infra\modules\reminder-schedule\main.tf-16-# context-attribute substitution does literal text matching for `<aws.scheduler.scheduled-time>` and never
infra\modules\reminder-schedule\main.tf-17-# found it once escaped, so the literal placeholder string reached the Lambda as
infra\modules\reminder-schedule\main.tf:18:# `scheduledTime`, and every producer/reconciliation/sweeper invocation failed validation
infra\modules\reminder-schedule\main.tf-19-# 100% of the time since the first `terraform apply` that created these schedules
infra\modules\reminder-schedule\main.tf-20-# (confirmed via `aws logs filter-log-events`, first occurrence 2026-08-20T14:41:39Z). Fixed
infra\modules\reminder-schedule\main.tf-21-# by writing `input` as a literal HCL string instead of `jsonencode(...)` for these 4
infra\modules\reminder-schedule\main.tf-22-# schedules specifically - never reintroduce `jsonencode()` here.

37:/** Hard cap on pages drained per invocation - matches the design's "pÃ¡gina lÃ³gica mÃ¡x. 200"
38: * per page with a bounded number of pages, so a pathological backlog can't make a single
39: * invocation run indefinitely; anything beyond this is picked up by the NEXT scheduled
40: * run (every 5 min for claims, daily for DST) rather than blocking this one. */
41:const MAX_PAGES = 25;
42:
43:const RECONCILIATION_EVENT_SCHEMA_ID = "https://expiration-tracker/schemas/events/reminder-reconciliation-event.v1.json";

45:export async function handler(event: unknown): Promise<void> {
46:  // m5-observability-design.md #2: EventBridge Scheduler producer, no upstream request to
47:  // inherit a correlationId from - new UUID per invocation.
48:  await runWithContext({ correlationId: randomUUID() }, async () => {
49:    // P2.1 (external audit 2026-09-11): `event` was previously typed (not runtime-validated)
50:    // as `ReminderReconciliationEvent` straight off the Lambda invocation - a TS annotation
51:    // enforces nothing at runtime. Same schema-registry pattern reminder-dispatch-handler.ts's
52:    // `DISPATCH_COMMAND_SCHEMA_ID` already uses for its own boundary, mirrored here.
53:    const { valid, errors } = defaultSchemaRegistry.validate(RECONCILIATION_EVENT_SCHEMA_ID, event);
54:    if (!valid) {
55:      logger.error("reminder-reconciliation schema-invalid event", { errors });
56:      throw new Error("schema-invalid ReminderReconciliationEvent");
57:    }
58:    await handleReconciliation(event as ReminderReconciliationEvent);
59:  });
60:}

62:async function handleReconciliation(event: ReminderReconciliationEvent): Promise<void> {
63:  const mode = event.mode;
64:
65:  const expiredClaimCandidates: ReminderOccurrence[] = [];
66:  const dstCandidates: FullDstCandidate[] = [];
67:
68:  if (mode === "CLAIMS") {
69:    // GSI6 is ALL-projected - each candidate row already IS the full ReminderOccurrence
70:    // item (see ExpiredClaimCandidate's doc comment), so no extra fetch is needed.
71:    // Pagination is drained (bug found by Codex implementation review: the first version
72:    // only ever read page 1, silently leaving any backlog over one page unprocessed).
73:    let cursor: string | undefined;
74:    for (let page = 0; page < MAX_PAGES; page++) {
75:      const result = await candidateSource.listExpiredClaims({ before: now(), cursor });
76:      expiredClaimCandidates.push(...(result.items as unknown as ReminderOccurrence[]));
77:      if (!result.cursor) break;
78:      cursor = result.cursor;
79:    }
80:  }
81:
82:  if (mode === "DST") {
83:    // ReminderMaterializer (M3.5) writes a WORKSTATE#DST_PENDING GSI6 pointer whenever a
84:    // trigger's schedule was computed at an ambiguous/nonexistent local time, OR whose
85:    // timeZone observes DST at all (see reminder-materializer.ts - broadened per Codex
86:    // implementation review: a non-ambiguous 09:00 reminder in a DST-observing zone can
87:    // still need re-evaluation after an offset change, not just literally-ambiguous ones).
88:    // This query finds those candidates; occurrences in a fixed-offset timeZone never
89:    // appear here at all.
90:    const windowStart = now();
91:    const windowEnd = new Date(Date.parse(windowStart) + 7 * 24 * 60 * 60_000).toISOString();
92:    let cursor: string | undefined;
93:    for (let page = 0; page < MAX_PAGES; page++) {
94:      const result = await candidateSource.listDstCandidates({ window: { start: windowStart, end: windowEnd }, cursor });
95:      for (const light of result.items) {
96:        const policy = await store.get<ReminderPolicy>(policyKey(light.tenantId, light.policyId));
97:        if (!policy) continue;
98:        const item = await store.get<{ PK: string; SK: string; dueDate: string; version: number }>(itemKey(authorizedTenantIdFromPersistedEntity(light), light.itemId));
99:        if (!item) continue;
100:        dstCandidates.push({
101:          tenantId: light.tenantId,
102:          itemId: light.itemId,
103:          itemVersion: item.version,
104:          itemDueDate: item.dueDate,
105:          policy,
106:        });
107:      }
108:      if (!result.cursor) break;
109:      cursor = result.cursor;
110:    }
111:  }
112:
113:  const result = await runReconciliation({ store, tableName, now, shardConfig }, { expiredClaimCandidates, dstCandidates });
114:  logger.info("reminder-reconciliation complete", { mode, scheduledTime: event.scheduledTime, ...result });
115:}

22:  get<T extends EntityKey = Record<string, unknown> & EntityKey>(key: EntityKey): Promise<T | undefined>;
23:  transactWrite(entries: TransactWriteEntry[]): Promise<void>;
24:}
25:
26:export interface ChasingDispatchCommand {
27:  messageVersion: 1;
28:  messageId: string;
29:  createdAt: string;
30:  correlationId: string;
31:  commandType: "document-chasing.dispatch.v1";
32:  tenantId: string;
33:  deduplicationKey: string;
34:  data: {
35:    subjectId: string;
36:    assignmentId: string;
37:    documentRequestId: string;
38:    occurrenceId: string;
39:    occurrenceVersion: number;
40:    tier: DocumentChasingTier;
41:    scheduledAt: string;
42:    documentRequestVersion: number;
43:  };
44:}
45:
46:export interface ChasingClaimDeps {
47:  store: ChasingProducerStore;
48:  tableName: string;
49:  now: () => string;
50:  claimTtlMs: number;
51:  newEventId: () => string;
52:  correlationId: () => string;
53:}
54:
55:export type ChasingClaimOutcome =
56:  | { kind: "CLAIMED"; command: ChasingDispatchCommand }
57:  | { kind: "SKIPPED_NOT_SCHEDULED" }
58:  | { kind: "LOST_CLAIM_RACE" };
59:
60:/** Equivalente ao corpo do loop de `runProducerTick` para o caminho reminder, mas para
61: * `DocumentChasingOccurrence`. Chamado com a base PK/SK jÃ¡ lida da linha do GSI3 (projeÃ§Ã£o
62: * KEYS_ONLY sempre inclui as chaves primÃ¡rias da tabela base, mesmo mecanismo jÃ¡ usado pelo
63: * caminho reminder). */
64:export async function claimChasingOccurrence(deps: ChasingClaimDeps, baseKey: EntityKey): Promise<ChasingClaimOutcome> {
65:  const occurrence = await deps.store.get<DocumentChasingOccurrence>(baseKey);
66:  if (!occurrence || occurrence.status !== "SCHEDULED") {
67:    return { kind: "SKIPPED_NOT_SCHEDULED" };
68:  }
69:
70:  const { occurrenceId } = occurrence;
71:  const tenantId = authorizedTenantIdFromPersistedEntity(occurrence);
72:  const claimExpiresAt = new Date(Date.parse(deps.now()) + deps.claimTtlMs).toISOString();
73:  const newVersion = occurrence.version + 1;
74:  const now = deps.now();
75:  const correlationId = deps.correlationId();
76:
77:  const command: ChasingDispatchCommand = {
78:    messageVersion: 1,
79:    messageId: deps.newEventId(),
80:    createdAt: now,
81:    correlationId,
82:    commandType: "document-chasing.dispatch.v1",
83:    tenantId,
84:    deduplicationKey: `${tenantId}|${occurrenceId}|${newVersion}`,
85:    data: {
86:      subjectId: occurrence.subjectId,
87:      assignmentId: occurrence.assignmentId,
88:      documentRequestId: occurrence.documentRequestId,
89:      occurrenceId,
90:      occurrenceVersion: newVersion,
91:      tier: occurrence.tier,
92:      scheduledAt: occurrence.scheduledAt,
93:      documentRequestVersion: occurrence.documentRequestVersion,
94:    },
95:  };
96:
97:  const event: DomainEvent = {
98:    specVersion: "1.0",
99:    eventId: deps.newEventId(),
100:    eventType: "DocumentChasingDispatchRequested",
101:    source: "expiration-tracker.document-chasing-producer",
102:    occurredAt: now,
103:    correlationId,
104:    tenantId,
105:    actor: { type: "SYSTEM" },
106:    aggregate: { type: "DocumentChasingOccurrence", id: occurrenceId, version: newVersion },
107:    data: command as unknown as Record<string, unknown>,
108:  };
109:  const outboxEntries: DynamoTransactPutEntry[] = [];
110:  appendToTransaction(outboxEntries, deps.tableName, event, "SQS_DOCUMENT_CHASING_DISPATCH_V1");
111:
112:  try {
113:    await deps.store.transactWrite([
114:      {
115:        Update: buildVersionedUpdate({
116:          tableName: deps.tableName,
117:          key: { PK: occurrence.PK, SK: occurrence.SK },
118:          tenantId,
119:          expectedVersion: occurrence.version,
120:          set: {
121:            status: "CLAIMED",
122:            claimedAt: deps.now(),
123:            claimExpiresAt,
124:            GSI6PK: GSI6PK_WORKSTATE_CLAIMED,
125:            GSI6SK: buildChasingClaimGsi6Sk(claimExpiresAt, tenantId, occurrenceId),
126:          },
127:        }),
128:      },
129:      ...outboxEntries,
130:    ]);
131:  } catch (err) {
132:    if (isTransactionCanceled(err)) {
133:      return { kind: "LOST_CLAIM_RACE" };
134:    }
135:    throw err;
136:  }
137:
138:  return { kind: "CLAIMED", command };
139:}

132:export class SchemaRegistry {
133:  private readonly ajv: Ajv2020;
134:  private readonly compiled = new Map<string, ValidateFunction>();
135:
136:  /** Takes an explicit list of already-loaded schema objects - no filesystem access. Callers
137:   * that need "every schema under schemas/" (CLI/tests) use
138:   * `schema-registry-disk.ts#loadAllSchemasFromDisk()` instead of constructing this directly
139:   * with an empty/missing list. */
140:  constructor(schemas: object[]) {
141:    this.ajv = new Ajv2020({ strict: true, allErrors: true });
142:    addFormats(this.ajv);
143:    // Two passes not needed here since all schemas are added before any compile() call below
144:    // (compile is lazy, triggered by the first validate() per schemaId) - $ref between
145:    // schemas resolves correctly regardless of list order.
146:    for (const schema of schemas) {
147:      const withId = schema as { $id?: string };
148:      if (withId.$id) {
149:        this.ajv.addSchema(schema, withId.$id);
150:      }
151:    }
152:  }
153:
154:  /** Validates `data` against the schema identified by its `$id`. Returns { valid, errors }. */
155:  validate(schemaId: string, data: unknown): { valid: boolean; errors: string[] } {
156:    let validateFn = this.compiled.get(schemaId);
157:    if (!validateFn) {
158:      const fn = this.ajv.getSchema(schemaId);
159:      if (!fn) {
160:        throw new Error(`Unknown schema $id: ${schemaId}`);
161:      }
162:      validateFn = fn;
163:      this.compiled.set(schemaId, validateFn);
164:    }
165:    const valid = validateFn(data) as boolean;
166:    const errors = (validateFn.errors ?? []).map(
167:      (e) => `${e.instancePath || "/"} ${e.message ?? "invalid"}`,
168:    );
169:    return { valid, errors };
170:  }
171:}
172:
173:/**
174: * Production runtime singleton - imported by Lambda handlers (e.g. reminder-dispatch-
175: * handler.ts). Built from statically-imported schema modules so esbuild inlines them as JS
176: * object literals into the bundle at build time, same fix as Redactor's
177: * schemas/sensitive-fields.json (Arquitetura axis round1, commit 494f4e5). Do NOT change
178: * this back to `new SchemaRegistry()` (dynamic directory walk) - that depends on
179: * `import.meta.url`, which is empty under the esbuild "cjs" bundle format
180: * (infra/lib/scoped-lambda-function.ts's bundleEntry) and would silently resolve zero
181: * schemas at real Lambda cold start. New schema added under schemas/ that a handler needs
182: * at runtime: add both the file AND a static import line above.
183: */
184:export const defaultSchemaRegistry = new SchemaRegistry([
185:  domainEventEnvelopeV1,
186:  commandEnvelopeV1,
187:  webhookInboxV1,
188:  notificationIntentCreatedV1,

The new `SCANLEASE#IN_PROGRESS` GSI6 pointer plus the independent five-minute CLAIMS pass eliminates dependence on rediscovering the minute through the producer lookback ([round-4-claude-revision.md:31](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\docs\architecture\reviews\reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping\round-4-claude-revision.md:31), [round-4-claude-revision.md:39](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\docs\architecture\reviews\reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping\round-4-claude-revision.md:39)). The current handler really does run CLAIMS every five minutes and already queries GSI6 ([reminder-reconciliation-handler.ts:1](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\src\runtime\aws\handlers\reminder-reconciliation-handler.ts:1), [reminder-reconciliation-handler.ts:68](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\src\runtime\aws\handlers\reminder-reconciliation-handler.ts:68), [reminder-reconciliation-handler.ts:75](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\src\runtime\aws\handlers\reminder-reconciliation-handler.ts:75)). The adapter already implements the required `GSI6PK = ... AND GSI6SK < ...` query shape ([dynamodb-reconciliation-candidate-source.ts:30](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\src\modules\reminder\persistence\dynamodb-reconciliation-candidate-source.ts:30)).

The role has both ordinary table writes and unrestricted Query/GetItem access to the GSI6 resource ([main.tf:298](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\infra\main.tf:298), [main.tf:310](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\infra\main.tf:310), [main.tf:312](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\infra\main.tf:312), [dynamo-table/main.tf:395](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\infra\modules\dynamo-table\main.tf:395)). Consequently, this new partition value needs no new IAM grant.

However, the header’s “exactly two roles” statement is no longer true ([reminder-reconciliation-handler.ts:4](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\src\runtime\aws\handlers\reminder-reconciliation-handler.ts:4)); Terraform documents exactly four authorized roles ([dynamo-table/main.tf:391](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\infra\modules\dynamo-table\main.tf:391)). Round 4 should not cite that stale comment as confirmation.

Formalizing a named sentinel beside `DomainEvent` is materially better than citing `Actor` as precedent. `DomainEvent.tenantId` is currently an unrestricted string ([events.ts:16](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\src\shared\contracts\events.ts:16), [events.ts:24](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\src\shared\contracts\events.ts:24)), and the outbox uses it to form `TENANT#${tenantId}#OUTBOX#...` and copies it into the record ([outbox.ts:126](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\src\shared\outbox\outbox.ts:126), [outbox.ts:129](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\src\shared\outbox\outbox.ts:129)). But “mapping disabled” does not prove that already-running scan/claim invocations have terminated. Round 4 explicitly allows proceeding even when visible or not-visible messages have not drained and calls draining non-blocking ([round-4-claude-revision.md:153](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\docs\architecture\reviews\reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping\round-4-claude-revision.md:153)). Apply B can therefore reactivate legacy scanning while an invocation admitted before Apply A is still claiming through the new path. The concurrent legacy/new claim window remains.

Leaving residual messages for a future re-enable is also not proven safe merely by idempotency ([round-4-claude-revision.md:161](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\docs\architecture\reviews\reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping\round-4-claude-revision.md:161)). Idempotency prevents duplicate state transitions; it does not establish that replaying arbitrarily old scan or claim work is semantically valid.
